column7: We establish a period comparison for a two-dimensional rational Hodge summand of type $(3,0)+(0,3)$ in a smooth projective threefold over $\mathbb Q$ with $h^{3,0}=1$. Given an algebraic projector onto the summand and a correspondence whose action on the motive of a rational weight-four newform is nonzero after projection to the summand, restriction to the holomorphic de Rham lines identifies motivic morphisms with maps between these lines. Fixing rational generators of the holomorphic de Rham lines determines a unique isomorphism of homological motives. Its Betti realization then yields an exact relation between geometric periods and two critical modular $L$-values. For the Fermat sextic, we construct the correspondence over $\mathbb Q$ and compute its Betti and de Rham actions, determining the scale from algebraic traces and cup-product pairings. Critical-value evaluations and, under mirror comparison and explicit continuation hypotheses, a continued genus-zero Gromov--Witten partition identity follow as corollaries.

column5: Christian Böhning; Hans-Christian Graf von Bothmer; Alena Pirutka; Zhijia Zhang
column6: Stable irrationality of quartic hypersurfaces
column7: We prove that a very general quartic hypersurface of any positive dimension over an uncountable algebraically closed field of characteristic different from 2 does not admit an integral decomposition of the diagonal, and in particular it is not stably rational.

column6: A negative answer to the final question in "Les petits cailloux"
column7: We consider polynomial-time computation over arbitrary structures, with unit cost for the primitive operations and relations and with nondeterministic witnesses consisting of arbitrary structure elements. We prove that every finite-signature structure with two distinct available elements and containing a binary operation $*$ and total unary operations $L,R$ such that $L(x*y)=x$ and $R(x*y)=y$ satisfies $P\ne NP$. The proof encodes an exponentially long computation in one element. An incorrect transition has a polynomial-size binary address, and hence the existence of an error is an $NBP$ problem. Existence of a correct accepting trace belongs to the mixed second level $Σ_2^{S,B}$, with an arbitrary-element existential block followed by a binary universal block. We obtain $EXP\subseteqΣ_2^{S,B}\subseteq PH$. A hypothetical equality $P=NP$ would collapse this hierarchy to $P$ and imply $P=EXP$, contradicting a direct deterministic diagonalization over the same structure. A simulation by function graphs extends the obstruction to every jointly injective binary primitive under the same assumptions on equality and available elements. Consequently no unary predicate on Malcev's free binary-tree algebra yields $P=NP$, with or without the projections. In contrast, starting from the author's unary example, we construct five infinite structures with binary operations and $P=NP$. These include an algebra with one binary operation and one constant, an expansion with an associative rectangular-band operation, and an algebra with one binary operation whose every row and column has infinite image.

column6: Normality in generalized Rudin spaces
column7: In \cite{Kojman2026}, Kojman generalized Mary Ellen Rudin's construction of a ZFC Dowker space to larger cardinals and gave a pcf-theoretic condition ensuring that the resulting spaces are collectionwise normal. A subsequent manuscript by Eisworth, Kojman, Lambie-Hanson, and Marun \cite{EKLM2026} develops the theory further and leaves open whether these generalized Rudin spaces can fail to be normal. We answer this question by proving that, for cardinals $μ<δ$ with $\operatorname{cf}(δ)=\aleph_0$, the generalized Rudin space $X(μ,δ)$ is normal if and only if $\operatorname{pp}(ν)<δ$ for every cardinal $ν\in(μ,δ)$ with $\operatorname{cf}(ν)=\aleph_0$. Given this characterization, known consistency results provide consistent examples of nonnormal generalized Rudin spaces.

column6: The norm formula in a Banach space and in its complete theory
column7: Let $h$ be the Hilbert norm on the real space $\ell_2(\mathbb{N})\oplus_2\ell_2(\mathbb{N})$, and put $q(u,v)=\sup_{i<j}|u_i+v_j|$. For each of Bollobás's additive norms $h+\varepsilon q$, $\varepsilon>0$, and for the quadratic norm $\sqrt{h^2+q^2}$, the norm formula $\lVert x+y\rVert$ is unstable on the renormed space and has no independence property in its complete theory. We approximate $q(x+y)$ uniformly on bounded Hilbert balls by truncating small coordinates. For $n$ fixed test vectors and thresholds, the number of threshold patterns of $q(x+y)$ as $y$ varies is bounded by a polynomial in $n$ when the support sizes of the test vectors and of $y$ are bounded. These estimates give finite fat-shattering dimension for the translates of $q$ at every positive scale. The norm formula on a space can be stable, unstable without the independence property, or have the independence property. We give an example in each of these three cases where the formula has the independence property in the complete theory, and an example in each of the first two cases where it lacks that property in the complete theory. All five spaces satisfy a common midpoint estimate for uniform convexity, and each admits an isomorphism to Hilbert space of distortion at most $\sqrt3$.

column5: Dominik Burek; Tymoteusz Chmiel; Sławomir Cynk; Marcin Oczko
column6: A projective Calabi--Yau threefold in characteristic 5 non-liftable to characteristic 0
column7: We construct a smooth projective Calabi--Yau threefold $X_5$ over $\mathbb F_5$ with $b_3(X_5)=0$ and $b_2(X_5)=31$. Consequently, $X_5$ has no smooth proper lifting to characteristic zero, including over ramified bases. To our knowledge, this is the first smooth projective Calabi--Yau threefold with this property in characteristic $p>3$. The threefold is a crepant resolution of the Kummer quotient of the self-fiber product of a rational elliptic surface. We prove the vanishing of its third Betti number by semistable reduction and point counts. A birational double-octic model gives a direct obstruction to lifting to the ring of Witt vectors of length two, through an explicit inconsistent system of linear equations for the branch data. We also determine the Hodge and crystalline cohomology: the threefold is infinitesimally rigid, its crystalline cohomology is torsion-free, and its third de Rham cohomology vanishes. Its Hodge-de Rham spectral sequence has exactly two nonzero differentials, both of rank one on the second page.

column6: The Levitt--Yoccoz gasket: dynamics, Hausdorff dimension and norm exponent
column7: In S.P.~Novikov's problem on plane sections of 3ply periodic surfaces, the author and I.\,A.~Dynnikov showed that, for the $μ$-cube, the directions lying in no stability zone form the union of a fractal set $N$, the Levitt--Yoccoz gasket (projectively equivalent to the Rauzy gasket), and of its images under the sign changes of the coordinates. $N$ is the limit set of a parabolic projective iterated function system $PΓ_N$ generated by a semigroup $Γ_N\subset SL_3(\mathbb Z)$, and each zone is labelled by a primitive integer vector, its soul. We show that $N$ is the global attractor of $PΓ_N$ and that the chain graphs of $PΓ_N$ and its Hutchinson map consist of a single node. Building on the theorem of Jiao--Li--Pan--Xu and Jurga that $\dim_H N$ equals the affinity exponent of $Γ_N$, we prove $1.6853<\dim_HN=\dim_BN<1.6854$. For some class of cut-out gaskets $K$, we bound $\overline{\dim}_B K$ from both sides by the norm exponent $s_N(Γ)$. The norm exponent $s_N$ of $G_N$, the counting exponent of the souls, is Baragar's exponent of the Markoff--Hurwitz equation $x_1^2+x_2^2+x_3^2+x_4^2=ax_1x_2x_3x_4$. We prove $2.4411\le s_N\le2.4465$, improving Baragar's bounds, and $\frac23 s_N\le\dim_H N\le\frac12(1+s_N)$, which proves a conjecture by Gamburd, Magee and Ronan; and we show that the exponent of the equation in six variables exceeds $3$, answering a question of Baragar. For the three-dimensional Levitt--Yoccoz gasket $G\subset\mathbb RP^3$ we prove $2.74\le s_N(Γ_G)\le2.777$ and $\dim_H G\le2.3885$. Finally, for the renormalization flow of Avila, Hubert and Skripchenko, we show that the invariant measure they introduce is the Gibbs measure at the parameter $s_N$ and that $s_N$ is the maximal entropy per unit time of the return map, attained only by this measure. So, the diffusion exponent of their chaotic plane sections is less than 0.7766.

column6: Prime values of linear forms and a quadratic form: one proof and two arithmetic applications
column7: Let $L_1,\dots,L_k\in \mathbb Z[x,y]$ be a system of linear polynomials whose homogeneous parts are pairwise linearly independent. Let $K=\mathbb Q(α)$ be an imaginary quadratic field. Utilizing the higher order Fourier analysis machinery of Green and Sawhney in their breakthrough work on the Gaussian prime conjecture, we show that if there are no local obstructions, then there are infinitely many $(x,y)\in \mathbb Z$ such that $L_1(x,y),\dots,L_k(x,y),$ and $N_{K/\mathbb Q}(x+yα)$ are simultaneously prime. We further establish an asymptotic formula which matches the prediction by the multivariate Bateman-Horn conjecture. We present two arithmetic applications of this prime counting result. First, we show that the Brauer--Manin obstruction is the only obstruction to weak approximation on a new family of varieties, including diagonal conic bundles all of whose degenerate fibres are defined over $\mathbb Q$ except one fibre that may be defined over an imaginary quadratic field. Second, we construct elliptic curves over $\mathbb Q$ with infinitely many quadratic twists of rank exactly two.

column6: Rigid Theories
column7: A structure is rigid if it admits no non-trivial automorphisms. We investigate an analogous invariance property for first-order theories, with relative interpretations playing the role of morphisms. A theory $T$ is called rigid if and only if every self-interpretation of $T$ is definably isomorphic to the identity interpretation. Extending work of Pakhomov and Zapryagaev (2020) on Presburger Arithmetic, we establish rigidity for Successor Arithmetic and Skolem Arithmetic (with respect to one-dimensional interpretations), True Arithmetic, and the theories of fields $\mathrm{RCF}$ and $\mathrm{ACF}$. By contrast, $\mathrm{PA}$ and $\mathrm{ZF}$ admit infinitely many self-interpretations, though both remain rigid with respect to (co-)retractions. Our main negative result is that $\mathrm{ZFC}$ has no consistent rigid extension in its own language. We compare rigidity with categoricity, model rigidity, completeness, and solidity, showing it to be independent of the first three, and indicate the relevance of rigidity to questions about semantic determinacy.

column5: Jonah Gaster; Didac Martinez-Granado; Christopher-Lloyd Simon
column6: Simple Length Multiplicity on X(n)
column7: We study multiplicity among lengths of simple closed geodesics on the principal congruence surfaces $X(n)=Γ(n)\backslash\mathbb{H}$. We show that for every $\varepsilon>0$ there are positive constants $n_\varepsilon,C_{\varepsilon}$ so that, for $n\ge n_\varepsilon$, there are at least $\exp((\frac{π^2}{12}-\varepsilon)n)$ simple closed geodesics on $X(n)$ of the same length $\ell<C_\varepsilon n$. We produce the same multiplicity for $λ$-length of simple arcs with distinct endpoints via the McShane identity, which is immediately relevant as the size of a McShane gap around such an arc is roughly the reciprocal square of its $λ$-length. Our method of proof relies on an independently interesting theorem about the McShane identity for $X(n)$: the total mass of the gaps of pants with two cusps tends to 1 as $n\to \infty$. We present a proof of this latter fact that relies on estimates for the speed of mixing provided by Selberg's 3/16-Theorem (discovered with the help of ChatGPT). We indicate several avenues for further investigation.

column6: A Diophantine definition of $\mathbb{Z}$ in $\mathbb{Q}$
column7: We prove that $\mathbb{Z}$ is a Diophantine subset of $\mathbb{Q}$. More precisely, there exist an integer $m\ge 1$ and a polynomial of total degree at most four in $m+1$ variables whose rational zero set projects onto $\mathbb{Z}$ under the first coordinate. We construct a Diophantine model of $\mathbb{Z}$ on an elliptic curve and use it to define real intervals with rational endpoints, each containing an integer. A denominator bound identifies a rational number in a sufficiently short interval with that integer. The key ingredients are a criterion for square denominators, obtained using the Tian--Yuan--Zhang genus-point criterion for congruent number elliptic curves, and a height bound from quaternionic abelian surfaces. The Green--Tao theorem supplies prime progressions needed to define squaring, and hence multiplication, in the model. Our proof is inspired by OpenAI's approach to Hilbert's tenth problem over $\mathbb{Q}$, but does not rely on the $2$-converse or $2$-adic Fontaine--Mazur results announced and invoked by OpenAI.

column6: Congruences Modulo 16, 32 and 64 for a Restricted Overpartition Function
column7: Let $\overline{t}^{(3)}(n)$ denote the number of overpartitions of $n$ in which consecutive parts differ by a multiple of $3$ unless the larger part is overlined, and the smallest part is overlined unless it is divisible by $3$. Using dissections of theta functions, we establish two infinite families of congruences modulo $32$ and $64$. We also obtain two residue formulas modulo $16$ and use them to derive four further infinite families of congruences modulo $16$. In particular, for every positive integer $M$ and nonnegative integer $n$, the residue of $\overline{t}^{(3)}(M^2(18n+12))$ modulo $16$ is $8$ if $6n+4$ is a square and $0$ otherwise.

column5: Stéphane Fischler; Li Lai; Johannes Sprang; Wadim Zudilin
column6: Many more odd zeta values are irrational
column7: We prove that for any sufficiently large odd integer $s$, there exist at least \[ 2.78 \, \sqrt{\frac{s \log\log s}{\log s}} \] irrational values among $ζ(3), ζ(5), \dots, ζ(s)$, where $ζ$ is the Riemann zeta function. This improves on the best known estimate by a constant factor times $\sqrt{ \log\log s}$. The proof combines the elimination technique and an arithmetic lemma of Fischler--Sprang--Zudilin, the hypergeometric constructions of Lai--Yu, and the Hankel determinant method that appeared in the proof that $ζ(5)$ is irrational posted by Fauzan on September 17, 2026.

column6: Admissibility of unbounded complexes of smooth representations
column7: Let $G$ be a $p$-adic Lie group and $k$ a field of characteristic $p$. We prove that a complex of smooth $k$-representations of $G$ has admissible cohomology if and only if it is globally admissible, i.e., its hypercohomology with respect to a torsion-free open compact pro-$p$ subgroup is finite dimensional in every degree. This extends the bounded-below and bounded-above comparison of Schneider--Sorensen to arbitrary unbounded complexes.

column6: Stationary Phase along Rays and the Determinant of Linearly Constrained Kloosterman Families
column7: We study the top-weight sheaf $\mathcal W_n$ of linearly constrained Kloosterman sums over finite fields of odd characteristic, of rank $r(n)=2^n-\binom n{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}$. A local Fourier-transform analysis describes wild monodromy at infinity along rays through nonescaping critical points and their quadratic characters, giving explicit Swan conductors and the escape locus. The resulting stationary-phase description yields a ray-theoretic proof of the geometric determinant. A reflection pairing and a Frobenius calculation at the tame endpoint recover the arithmetic determinant $\det\mathcal W_n\simeq\mathcal L_ψ(-2^{n-1}λ^{-1}\sum_i h_i)\otimes\overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell(-(n+1)r(n)/2)$. We obtain reciprocity for exterior-power Frobenius traces, the exact distribution of normalized determinants, and spectral compression on symmetric loci. Assuming the ambient connected-monodromy theorem from companion work, we determine the monodromy of the geometric generic ray. Further results include bounds for complete exponential sums, conductor identities for selected parameter curves, and the Euler characteristic of the parameter torus. Rank-two boundary conormal calculations are separated from higher-codimension characteristic-cycle recursions, which remain conditional on explicit microlocal hypotheses.

column5: Jinping Li; Yueming Zhong; Yangbiao Zhou
column6: Integral Exponential Series: Fibonacci Weights and Implicit Equations
column7: We apply classical prime-power congruence criteria to two families of exponential series. For the Fibonacci numbers $F_n$, we characterize the polynomials $P\in\Z[T]$ for which $\exp(\sum_{n\ge1}P(F_n)x^n/n)$ has integer coefficients: this holds if and only if $P$ is even and $P(0)\equiv P(1)\equiv P(2)\pmod5$. In particular, $5$ is the least positive multiplier for each positive even power of $F_n$, and the series with weights $5F_n^{2k}$ has degree $5^{k-1}$ over $\Q(x)$ for $k\ge1$. For $R_n(y)\in\Z[y]$ satisfying $R_{pn}(y)\equiv R_n(y)\pmod p$ for every prime $p$ and every $n\ge1$, we prove that $H(x,y)=\exp(\sum_{n\ge1}R_n(y)^n x^n/n)$ belongs to $\Z[y][[x]]$ and that $A(x)=H(x,A(x))$ has a unique integral solution. For $q\in \Z$, taking $R_n(y)=q^n+y$ proves the conjecture in OEIS A163138; the Fibonacci result proves the conjecture in A207969 and A207970. For the implicit family with indeterminate $q$, the coefficient of $x^n$ has degree $n^2$, leading coefficient $1/n$, and nonnegative integer coefficients in the binomial basis, for every $n\ge1$.

column6: Counting circles in Kleinian circle packings
column7: Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a bounded Kleinian circle packing with symmetry group $Γ$, and let $N_{\mathcal{P}}(T)$ denote the number of circles in $\mathcal{P}$ of radius at least $T^{-1}$. We obtain an asymptotic formula for $N_{\mathcal{P}}(T)$ in which the eigenvalues of the Laplace operator below the continuous spectrum contribute a finite sum of main terms, with an error term having the same exponent as in the counting theorem of Lax--Phillips for $Γ$-orbits in $\mathbb H^3$.

column6: Postcritically Finite Unicritical Polynomials over CM Fields
column7: A rational map of degree at least two is postcritically finite (PCF) if every critical point has a finite forward orbit. For the unicritical family $f_{d,c}(z)=z^d+c$ with $d\ge2$, we call $c$ a PCF parameter if $f_{d,c}$ is PCF. As discussed by Baker and DeMarco, these parameters are analogous to $j$-invariants of elliptic curves with complex multiplication. For every $d\ge2$, we determine which PCF parameters lie in a CM field. The same list gives all PCF parameters over the maximal abelian extension of $\mathbb{Q}$. This extends the classifications of Noytaptim and Petsche over the maximal totally real extension of $\mathbb{Q}$ and of Ferraguti and Pagano over quadratic number fields. The proof uses the totally real classification in degree two, orbit bounds, Kronecker's theorem, Goksel's unit theorem, Lam--Leung's short-sum classification, cyclotomic averages, and known irreducibility results.

column6: Optimal Sample Complexity for Genus-Two Zeta Functions from Noisy Random Euler Products
column7: We study exact recovery of the Hasse--Weil zeta numerator from repeated noisy observations of a randomized Euler product. For a genus-two curve over $\mathbb{F}_q$, we attach independent symmetric signs to its closed points and observe the logarithm of the resulting product at $t_q=c/\sqrt q$, where $0<c<1/\sqrt{12}$ is fixed. For every fixed, known additive noise density $f$ satisfying $\sqrt{f}\in H^1(\mathbb{R})$, we prove that the minimax number of independent observations required for exact recovery with error probability at most $δ$ has order $q^4\log(1/δ)$. No moment condition is imposed on the noise, so the result includes Cauchy readout. The upper bound estimates the phase of an empirical characteristic function and uses the separation of the integral Weil coefficients. The matching lower bound compares the full observation laws for two actual curves with ordinary, absolutely simple Jacobians. It combines a binomial comparison with a uniform bound on the closed-point tail. Thus access to the full observations does not improve the sample order attained by the phase estimator. The result concerns the information in a specified observation channel. It does not assume an efficient implementation of that channel.

column6: p-adic Height Pairing through Higher Class Field Theory: Part I
column7: We construct a p-adic height pairing for curves with split degenerate stable reduction over the prime p using the higher class field theory of Kato-Saito. We then show this pairing coincide with the standard Coleman-Gross p-adic height pairing when extended to the semistable reduction case using methods by Besser and Vologodsky.

column6: The solutions of the Diophantine equation $(2^{k}-1)(3^{l}-1)=7^{m}-1$
column7: In this paper, we will show that the positive integer triple $(k,l,m)$ satisfying the equation in the title is $(2,1,1).$

column6: A sharp bound for the $a$-number of a cyclic cover of $\mathbb{P}^1$
column7: Let $X$ be a smooth projective curve of genus $g$ over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic $p>2$. We give upper bounds for the $a$-number $a(X)$ when $X$ is hyperelliptic or, more generally, a tame cyclic cover of the projective line. For hyperelliptic curves, writing $g=pm+r$ with $0\le r<p$ and $n=(p-1)/2$, we prove the sharp bound $a(X)\le nm+\min\{n,r\}$. For tame cyclic covers, we refine previously known upper bounds and give curves attaining the resulting bound in infinitely many genera in characteristics $3$ and $5$. The proofs combine an alternating pairing on the bundle of locally exact differentials, originally due to Raynaud, with an explicit polynomial description of the Cartier operator. We also produce an explicit locus of hyperelliptic curves $X$ with $a(X)\ge a_g$, where $\frac{a_g}{g}$ converges to $\frac{p-1}{2p}$ as $g$ goes to $\infty$, whose dimension grows linearly with the genus $g$. These families exhibit excess intersections of the Torelli locus with loci of large $a$-number in the moduli space of principally polarized abelian varieties.

column6: Strong Lyndon Interpolation for Multi-Modal Logics with Converses: A Constructive Approach with Tree Sequents
column7: Grammar logics with converses are multi-modal logics that generalize tense logics and whose frame conditions are determined by context-free production rules. We study the strong Lyndon interpolation property (strong LIP) for these logics, which requires interpolants to respect both the polarities of propositional atoms and the indices of modalities. We show that the strong LIP properly strengthens the Lyndon interpolation property over grammar logics, since it fails for certain grammar logics with bridge axioms, i.e., path axioms relating modalities with distinct indices. We then prove that every bridge-free grammar logic, possibly extended with seriality axioms, has the strong LIP. This class includes the multi-modal tense logics obtained by imposing any combination of seriality, reflexivity, transitivity, symmetry, and Euclideanity on each pair of converse modalities. Our proof is constructive and purely syntactic, and is based on tree sequent calculi. Because standard methods for computing interpolants with tree and nested sequents may introduce modalities whose indices are not common to both sides of an implication, we introduce a novel tripartite partition method. It sorts the labels of a proof into common labels and labels private to the left or right component, and only lets relational atoms pointing to common labels contribute modalities to interpolants. Given a proof of an implication, our method computes a strong Lyndon interpolant together with proofs of its correctness.

column6: The Evertse-Ferretti interval result for a set of weights, and the exponent $1/2$ in three complexity bounds
column7: The interval result of Evertse and Ferretti (2013) concerns a tuple $L$ of linear forms and one tuple $c$ of weights. It says that the parameters $Q$ for which the twisted height $H_{L,c,Q}$ has a small value outside an exceptional subspace $T(L,c)$ lie in $O(δ^{-2}\logδ^{-1})$ intervals $[Q_i,Q_i^ω)$. We prove this for a whole set $\mathcal{C}$ of weights with the same forms. At most $J$ subspaces $T(L,c)$ occur, where $J$ depends only on the dimension and on the number of places, and one family of $O(δ^{-2}\logδ^{-1})$ intervals serves every $c\in\mathcal{C}$ at once. Neither count depends on $\mathcal{C}$. In applications of Bugeaud-Evertse type the solutions are sorted into about $\varepsilon^{-1}$ classes with the same forms and different weights, and one application now serves all classes. We deduce three complexity bounds. For a real algebraic irrational number $ξ$, the number $p(n,ξ,b)$ of blocks of length $n$ in its base-$b$ expansion satisfies $\limsup p(n,ξ,b)/(n(\log n)^η)=\infty$ for every $η<1/2$; Bugeaud and Evertse proved this for $η<1/11$. The same holds for the continued fraction expansion of an algebraic number of degree at least three, and for the steering word of $(3/2)^n$. We explain why $1/2$ is the limit of the method. All results are machine-verified in Lean~4.

column5: Shreyas Pai; Kaneenika Sinha; Naman Thakkar
column6: Central limit theorems for Frobenius, Hecke and Kloosterman angles
column7: The Frobenius angles of non-CM elliptic curves and the Hecke angles of non-CM newforms are equidistributed with respect to the Sato--Tate measure, while for Kloosterman angles, this is known on average over natural families. We study the fluctuations around these laws in large families, for smooth test functions. We prove an unconditional central limit theorem for Frobenius angles of elliptic curves for a much larger class of test functions than previously considered; earlier results assumed the Riemann hypothesis for $L$-functions of Hecke eigenforms of full level. This result follows from a general framework, developed here, which yields Gaussian moments for statistics of sequences in $[0,1]$ varying over families. In this framework, independence is replaced by two quantitative conditions: approximate independence at distinct indices, and convergence of the family averages to the Weyl limits at a suitable rate. As further applications, we extend central limit theorems for Kloosterman angles and for Hecke angles of newforms to larger classes of test functions, the latter with the weight and the level varying simultaneously. We also treat the dilated angles $αθ$ for integers $α\geq2$, whose limiting distribution is uniform. Finally, we discuss sharp statistics, obtaining a central limit theorem for Hecke angles and explaining the obstruction for the other two families.

column6: Minimising Disquotational Truth
column7: We present a new axiomatic theory of disquotational truth based on the theory of positive disquotation PUTB. Formulated in classical logic, PUTB restricts the T-schema to positive sentences and satisfies key epistemic desiderata (semantic conservativity and trustworthiness). However, it fares poorly in proof-theoretic strength compared to reflective truth frameworks. To address this, we propose a new theory of positive disquotation aimed at axiomatizing its least fixed-point model. Without requiring additional resources, we achieve this by incorporating ill-founded reasoning under suitable soundness restrictions, applying the tools of cyclic proof theory to axiomatic theories of truth. The resulting theory, CPUTB, is sound relative to the minimal fixed-point model and proves the same arithmetical theorems as the impredicative theory ID1.

column5: Sutirtha Datta; Sourav Ghosh; Aniruddha Maji; Antara Manik
column6: Matrix Waring Problem in finite fields with coefficients from $\mathrm{GL}(2, \mathbb{F}_p)$
column7: Let $k$ be a fixed positive integer and $p$ be an odd prime such that $\gcd(p-1,k)=1$. For sufficiently large primes $p$, we show that the equation $AX^k+BY^k=C$ has solutions $X,Y \in \mathrm{GL}(2, \mathbb{F}_p)$, where $A$ and $B$ are fixed matrices in $\mathrm{GL}(2, \mathbb{F}_p)$, and $C$ is a fixed matrix in $\mathrm{M}(2,\mathbb{F}_p).$ Our proof relies on Fourier analysis over $\mathrm{GL}(2, \mathbb{F}_p).$

column6: Proof of the Quasi Riemann Hypothesis using $\mathbb Q[i]$
column7: Using quartic Gauss sums in place of the cubic Gauss sums in OpenAI's original proof, we prove that the Dedekind $ζ$-function $ζ_{\mathbb Q(i)}(s)$ of $\mathbb Q(i)$ has no zeros in the half-plane $\Re s>599/600$, thereby obtaining the same zero-free half-plane for the Riemann $ζ$-function.We obtain the upper bound for the smoothed sum by applying Poisson summation twice and using the functional equation of the quartic Kubota series of angular weight $1$.In the Mellin representation, a zero-density bound for the family of quartic characters controls the terms from nonprincipal characters,and a residue and a lattice average over fourth powers give the main term.

column5: Jos{é} F. Fernando; Riccardo Ghiloni; Wiesław Pawłucki
column6: Strict $\mathcal{C}^\infty$-triangulation of subanalytic sets in low dimensions
column7: Let $R$ be a real closed field expanded by an o-minimal structure, let $A$ be a definable, closed and bounded subset of $R^n$ and let $p$ be a positive integer. It was recently shown in \cite{pa2} that $A$ admits a strict ${\mathcal C}^p$-triangulation $({\mathcal T},h)$, i.e., there exist a finite simplicial complex ${\mathcal T}$ in $R^n$ and a homeomorphism $h:|{\mathcal T}|\to A$ that is definable and of class ${\mathcal C}^p$. The aim of this article is to analyze a generalization of the notion of strict ${\mathcal C}^p$-triangulation of subanalytic sets to the case $p=\infty$. Examples in dimension $n=3$ show that such a generalization is not always possible within subanalytic geometry, where the class ${\mathcal C}^\infty$ is equivalent to the class ${\mathcal C}^ω$. We formulate the conjecture that strict ${\mathcal C}^\infty$-triangulations of subanalytic sets always exist in the wider o-minimal structure $\mathbb{R}_{{\rm an},\exp}$, generated by subanalytic sets and the exponential function. We check the conjecture for all subanalytic subsets of $\mathbb{R}^n$ when $n\leq 3$, and prepare tools to address the conjecture for arbitrary $n$. We also apply the obtained strict ${\mathcal C}^\infty$-triangulation results to approximate subanalytic continuous mappings $f:X\to Y$ between subanalytic sets $X\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ and $Y\subset\mathbb{R}^m$ by ${\mathcal C}^\infty$-mappings $g:X\to Y$ definable in the o-minimal structure $\mathbb{R}_{{\rm an},\exp}$, with respect to the strong Whitney ${\mathcal C}^0$ topology. If the continuous mapping $f:X\to Y$ is not necessarily subanalytic, we can still approximate it by ${\mathcal C}^\infty$ mappings $g:X\to Y$.

column6: Free Gödel algebras over Gödel hoops
column7: We give an explicit description of the left adjoint $F$ of the forgetful functor $U\colon\mathsf{GAlg}\to\mathsf{GHoops}$ from Gödel algebras to Gödel hoops. If $H$ is a Gödel hoop with a least element $m$, then $F(H)$ is the direct product of the Gödel algebra obtained by adjoining a new bottom element to $H$ and of $H$ itself, regarded as a Gödel algebra with bottom element $m$. For an arbitrary Gödel hoop $H$, we glue these products along the principal filters of $H$, and we describe the operations of $F(H)$, the action of $F$ on homomorphisms and the unit of the adjunction. As an application, we show that the unit of the adjunction $F\dashv U$ is not cartesian, and that the same holds for BL-algebras and basic hoops. Moreover, the semi-abelian categories of Gödel hoops and of basic hoops are not equivalent to the slice categories of Gödel algebras and of BL-algebras over their initial object. Thus, in contrast with the cases of Wajsberg hoops and of product hoops, the free-forgetful adjunctions between Gödel algebras and Gödel hoops, and between BL-algebras and basic hoops, do not give rise to ideally exact contexts.

column6: Higher moments of twisted Kloosterman sums and the arithmetic of algebraic varieties
column7: For an odd prime $p,$ consider the affine varieties $X_k: \sum\limits_{i=1}^{k}(x_i+x_i^{-1})=0$ over the finite field $\F_p.$ In this paper, a key feature of our work is arithmetic interpretation between the higher power moments of Kloosterman sums, modular forms and arithmetic geometry of the varieties $X_5$ and $X_6$ through their rational point counts. Our main results provide two distinct explicit formulas for the point count $\#X_5(\F_p).$ In the first formula, we express $\#X_5(\F_p)$ in terms of Fourier coefficients of modular forms and a certain weighted average of fourth power twisted Kloosterman moments, where the average is taken over multiplicative characters. We further establish an identity expressing this weighted average of fourth power moment of twisted Kloosterman sums in terms of fifth power quadratic twisted Kloosterman moment, together with Fourier coefficients of modular forms. Moreover, we derive an independent expression for the same average with different weight directly in terms of Fourier coefficients of modular forms. In the second identity for $\#X_5(\F_p)$, we express this purely in terms of Fourier coefficients of two modular forms. Moreover, we express $\#X_6(\F_p),$ in terms of Fourier coefficients of three modular forms. For these two expressions of $\#X_5(\F_p)$ and $\#X_6(\F_p),$ our approach is based on an identity that relates the point counts of $X_k$ to the $k$-th power moments of Kloosterman sum and its quadratic twist.

column6: Strong Completeness of Provability Logic for Languages of size at most continuum
column7: We investigate the strong completeness of $\mathrm{GL}(\mathbb P)$ for an infinite set of propositional variables $\mathbb P$ over ordinal spaces equipped with the interval topology $\mathcal{I}_1$. For every infinite cardinal $κ$, we consider the set \[ Γ_κ= \{\Diamond p_ξ:ξ<κ\} \cup \{\Box(p_ξ\to\Diamond p_η):ξ<η<κ\}, \] and prove that $Γ_κ$ has a model on an ordinal space with $\mathcal{I}_1$ if and only if $κ\nrightarrow_{\mathrm{ipath}}(ω)^2_{ω,<ω}$. We also prove that if $|\mathbb P|<\mathfrak p$, then $\mathrm{GL}(\mathbb P)$ is strongly complete with respect to $(ω^ω+1,\mathcal I_1)$. Finally, we establish the strong completeness of $\mathrm{GL}(\mathbb P)$ with respect to the same space whenever $|\mathbb P|=\aleph_1$.

column6: Propositional Dynamic Logic without tests does not have Craig Interpolation
column7: It was shown recently by Borzechowski et al. (2026) that Propositional Dynamic Logic (PDL) has Craig Interpolation. Whether test-free PDL, i.e. PDL without the `?' operator, has interpolation remained open. Here we answer this question in the negative with a counterexample: a test-free PDL validity for which no test-free interpolant exists. The validity only uses one atomic program and the Kleene star, so it implies that the basic modal logic K extended with the reflexive transitive closure does not have interpolation, as previously shown by Studer (2009). The example was originally obtained using LLMs and Lean. We describe our methodology and provide links to all prompts, LLM output summaries as well as the Lean proof.

column6: Finiteness of strongly reflective modular forms
column7: Let $Γ\subset\mathrm{O}^+(n,2)$ be a rational arithmetic group with $n\geq 3$. A non-constant modular form for $Γ$ is called strongly reflective if its zero divisor is a reduced union of mirrors of reflections in $Γ$. We show that, up to conjugation and multiplication by a nonzero scalar, there are only finitely many strongly reflective modular forms. As a consequence, we establish the finiteness of holomorphic automorphic products of singular weight. These results answer a question posed by Borcherds in 1995 and settle a conjecture of Gritsenko--Nikulin from 1998. As an application, up to conjugation, we prove the finiteness of $Γ$ whose corresponding algebra of modular forms is freely generated. The key ingredient is a uniform upper bound on the covolume of $Γ$, obtained by adapting the higher-rank lattice convergence theorem of Abért et al. to the study of the degrees of reflective branch divisors.

column6: Estimates of short exponential sums with primes in major arcs
column7: When solving a number of additive problems with almost equal summands, along with estimating short trigonometric sums with primes of the form $$ S_k(α;x,y)=\sum_{x-y<n\le x}Λ(n)e(αn^k), $$ on the minor arcs, estimates of these sums on the major arcs are also needed, except in a small neighborhood of their centers, as well as an asymptotic formula in a small neighborhood of the center of the major arcs. In this paper, using the second moment of Dirichlet $L$-functions on the critical line, for $S_k(α;x,y)$ on the major arcs $\mathfrak{M}(\mathscr{L}^b)$, $τ=y^5x^{-2}\mathscr{L}^{-b_1}$, $\mathscr{L} =\ln xq$, except in a small neighborhood of their centers $|α-\frac{a}{q}|>\left(2πk^2x^{k-2}y^2\right)^{-1}$, for $y\ge x^{1-\frac{1}{2k-1+η_k}}\mathscr{L}^{c_k}$, $$ η_k=\frac{2}{4k-5+2\sqrt{(2k-2)(2k-3)}}, \qquad c_k= \frac{2A+22+\left(\frac{2\sqrt{2k-3}}{\sqrt{2k-2}}-1\right)b_1}{2\sqrt{(2k-2)(2k-3)}-(2k-3)}, $$ a nontrivial estimate of the form $$ S_k(α;x,y)\ll y\mathscr{L}^{-A}, $$ is obtained, where $A$, $b_1$, $b$ are arbitrary fixed positive numbers, and an asymptotic formula is proved in a small neighborhood of the centers of the major arcs.

column6: Congruences involving the products of three binomial coefficients II
column7: Let $p$ be an odd prime, $a,m\in\Bbb Z_{(p)}$ and $a(a+1)m\not\equiv 0\pmod p$. In this paper, we deduce the congruence for $(\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{\binom{2k}k\binom ak\binom{-1-a}k}{m^k}) (\sum_{k=0}^{p-2}\frac{\binom{2k}k\binom ak\binom{-1-a}k}{m^k(k+1)})$ modulo $p^3$. As applications we obtain many congruences for \begin{align*}&\sum_{k=0}^{(p-1)/2}\frac{\binom{2k}k^3} {m^k(k+1)^r},\quad \sum_{k=0}^{p-2}\frac{\binom{2k}k^2\binom{4k}{2k}}{m^k(k+1)^r}, \quad \sum_{k=0}^{p-2}\frac{\binom{2k}k\binom{3k}k\binom{6k}{3k}} {m^k(k+1)^r}\quad(r=1,2,3) \\&\sum_{k=0}^{(p-1)/2}k^j\frac{\binom{2k}k^3} {m^k},\quad \sum_{k=0}^{p-1}k^j\frac{\binom{2k}k^2\binom{4k}{2k}}{m^k}, \quad \sum_{k=0}^{p-1}k^j\frac{\binom{2k}k\binom{3k}k\binom{6k}{3k}} {m^k}\quad(j=2,3) \end{align*} modulo $p^3$, which confirm the author's conjectures and improve previous results modulo $p^2$.

column6: Modular representations of reductive $p$-adic groups and the kernel of the trace map
column7: The trace map of a finite group gives a perfect duality between conjugacy classes and irreducible complex representations. For reductive $p$-adic groups, an analogous duality holds due to the classical work of Bernstein, Deligne and Kazhdan. In this paper, we study this trace map for modular representations of reductive $p$-adic groups in characteristic $\ell\ne p$. The failure of the duality is measured by the kernel of the trace map on the cocenter of the ``big Hecke algebra''. Our main theorem expresses this kernel in terms of corresponding kernels for finite-dimensional Hecke algebras associated with normalizers of parahoric subgroups in suitable central quotients of Levi subgroups, reducing a problem on infinite-dimensional algebras to finite-dimensional ones. We also show that projective representations provide a natural complementary subspace on the compact part of the cocenter. For affine Hecke algebras, we prove the naive-kernel conjecture over algebraically closed fields of arbitrary characteristic and for arbitrary compatible nonzero parameters, including unequal parameters and roots of unity.

column6: Differential properties of Drinfeld modular forms
column7: We study the action of vector fields on the Drinfeld symmetric spaces on de Rham classes of the generic Drinfeld module. The resulting Kodaira-Spencer map is an isomorphism, and is described by the Jacobian matrix \(J := (\frac{\partial g_{j}}{\partial ω_{i}})_{1 \leq i,j \leq r}\), where the \(g_{j}\) are the basic coefficient modular forms of rank \(r\). We show that \(J\) is the matrix inverse of the period matrix \(P\) that results from the de Rham theory of Drinfeld modules. We define the notion of Drinfeld modular differential form, which generalizes the transformation behavior of Drinfeld modular forms from functions to differential \(n\)-forms on the Drinfeld symmetric space \(Ω^{r}\). The algebra \(\mathbf{M}^{(*)} = \bigoplus_{0 \leq n < r} \mathbf{M}^{(n)}\) of all such is provided with a Serre derivation \(D \colon \mathbf{M}^{(n)} \to \mathbf{M}^{(n+1)}\) from \(n\)-forms to \((n+1)\)-forms, where \(\mathbf{M}^{(0)} = \mathbf{M}\) is the algebra of customary modular forms for \(\mathrm{GL}(r, \mathbb{F}_{q}[T])\). We determine the structure of \(\mathbf{M}^{(*)}\), which turns out to be the exterior algebra \(\bigwedge (\mathbf{M}^{(1)})\) of the \(\mathbf{M}\)-module \(\mathbf{M}^{(1)}\).

column6: Finite multiple harmonic sums and lower-truncated $p$-adic multiple zeta-star values
column7: We introduce lower-truncated $p$-adic multiple zeta-star values and construct their harmonic regularizations. We show that they are independent of the branch of the $p$-adic logarithm and satisfy harmonic product relations. We express finite multiple harmonic sums as alternating convolutions of harmonic-regularized $p$-adic multiple zeta values and lower-truncated $p$-adic multiple zeta-star values. This gives a $p$-adic analogue of the classical truncation identity, which reduces to the inversion relation between ordinary and star harmonic-regularized values when the truncation point is $1$. For truncation point $p$, it relates finite multiple zeta values to $p$-adic multiple zeta values.

column6: Rohrbach's Conjecture for Finite Groups
column7: Rohrbach's conjecture holds for finite groups. In fact, there is an absolute constant $C$ such that, for every finite group $G$, every positive integer $h$, and all nonnegative real numbers $α_1,\ldots,α_h$ with $α_1+\cdots+α_h=1$, there are subsets $A_1,\ldots,A_h\subseteq G$ satisfying \[ G=A_1\cdots A_h, \qquad |A_1|\leq |G|^{α_1}, \qquad |A_i|\leq C|G|^{α_i}\quad(2\leq i\leq h). \] Consequently, for every $h$ there is a constant $c_h$ such that every finite group $G$ has a subset $A$ with \[ A^h=G\qquad\text{and}\qquad |A|\leq c_h|G|^{1/h}. \]

column6: Permutation polynomials of given index up to quasi-multiplicative equivalence
column7: Let $q$ be a prime power and let $\ell$ be a divisor of $q-1$. We classify the permutation polynomials of $\mathbb F_q$ of polynomial index exactly $\ell$ up to quasi-multiplicative equivalence $G(X)\equiv uF(vX^d)\pmod{X^q-X}$, where $u,v\in\mathbb F_q^*$ and $\gcd(d,q-1)=1$, and we count the classes. For polynomials vanishing at $0$, the classes are the orbits of an explicit finite group on vectors of values at the $\ell$-th roots of unity. Through the permutation it induces on the roots of unity, each orbit lies over a double coset of the symmetric group $S_\ell$ with respect to its translation subgroup and an explicit affine group, and the stabilizers are explicit. For polynomials with nonzero constant term the action is free. Burnside's lemma, Möbius inversion over the coefficient support and congruences along the cycles of affine permutations give an exact formula for the number of classes. For fixed $\ell\geqslant2$ these numbers are quasi-polynomials in $s=(q-1)/\ell$ of degree at most $\ell-1$, with period dividing $\ell$ for odd $\ell$ and $2\ell$ for even $\ell$; for polynomials vanishing at $0$ the degree is exactly $\ell-1$, and we determine the leading coefficient. For odd prime $\ell$ and for $\ell=4$ the counts are given in closed form. For index four we also count the binomials and trinomials at each admissible coefficient support. The sums of two binomial counts that occur are expressed through quartic Jacobi sums and Frobenius traces of elliptic curves and of a curve of genus two; one of the elliptic curves is the reduction of the curve $Y^2=X^3+8X^2+32X$, which has no complex multiplication over $\mathbb Q$. The trinomial counts are expressed through quartic cyclotomic numbers and these sums. All these terms cancel when the counts with a fixed residue of the vanishing order modulo $s$ are added.

column6: A completely decomposable modular Jacobian of dimension $1777$
column7: We exhibit a congruence subgroup $Γ\subset\operatorname{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$ of level $120$ and index $23040$ whose modular curve $X_Γ$ has genus $1777$ and whose Jacobian is isogenous over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$ to a product of elliptic curves. This surpasses the previous record of a completely decomposable complex Jacobian of dimension $1297$ found by Ekedahl and Serre in $1993$.

column6: Mathematical foundations for symmetric programming and reasoning
column7: We develop a mathematical abstraction for uniformly exploiting symmetries in programming and reasoning based on the mathematical proof principle `without-loss-of-generality' (w.l.o.g.). Given: group actions that describe symmetries of the input and the output; and a canoniser, which captures how arbitrary inputs get sent to canonical ones, our construction extends any function from the canonical inputs to the whole domain. We characterise the conditions on the canonisers which guarantee that the construction gives the unique equivariant (i.e. symmetry-preserving) extension. Furthermore, we adapt the construction to a dependently-typed setting, where it captures traditional symmetric w.l.o.g. arguments via the Curry-Howard correspondence. Finally, we extend the construction to algebraic data types, where the symmetries of the constructors both uniquely determine the symmetries of the data type and pave the way for efficient execution.

column5: Alexander Kozachinskiy; Hector Pasten; Xavier Vidaux
column6: Why should $\mathbb{Z}$ be Diophantine in $\mathbb{Q}$?
column7: We give a Diophantine definition of the integers in the rational numbers conditional on the $abc$ conjecture, Dickson's conjecture, and finiteness of $2$-primary parts of Shafarevich--Tate groups. We also discuss some consequences of the existence of a Diophantine definition of the integers in the rational numbers. The goal of this work is to serve as an entry point to recent developments around Hilbert's tenth problem for the rational numbers.

column6: On the multidimensional polynomial Szemerédi theorem
column7: We study the multidimensional polynomial Szemerédi theorem over prime fields. Let $P_1,\dots,P_m\in\F_p[t]^k$ be block independent vector polynomials of degree at most $d$, with $P_i(0)=0$ for every $i$. We prove that there is a constant $c=c(k,m,d)>0$ such that, for every sufficiently large prime $p$, every set $A\subset\F_p^k$ with $|A|\ge p^{k-c}$ contains a configuration $x,x+P_1(t),\dots,x+P_m(t)$ with $t\in\F_p\setminus\{0\}$.

column6: Covering numbers and pcf theory
column7: We develop a general technique for deriving covering theorems from pcf-theoretic information by refining sequences of partitions. The method gives a direct proof of Shelah's cov vs. pp theorem and analogous results for diagonal coverings associated with normal ideals and covering modulo arbitrary $σ$-complete ideals, where $σ$ is regular and uncountable. In each setting, we characterize the covering invariant through pseudopowers, true cofinalities of reduced products of progressive sets, and appropriate notions of cofinality in (possible non-progressive) intervals of regular cardinals.

column6: Solovay's Construction via Proof Search
column7: Solovay's celebrated result establishes the arithmetical completeness of GL by embedding Kripke models into arithmetic. We provide an alternative proof of the arithmetical completeness of GL, in which we instead embed failed proof searches into arithmetic. Our methodology requires only a well-behaved sequent calculus and does not rely on completeness with respect to Kripke semantics or any of its variants. This approach is particularly interesting for logics that do not behave well semantically, such as ER, for which we also provide a new proof of arithmetical completeness.

column6: On transformations in the Second Painlevé family
column7: We complete the classification of algebraic relations among solutions of equations in the second Painlevé family $P_{II}(α): y''=2y^3+ty+α$, where $α\in\mathbb{C}$. More precisely, we prove that if $y_1,\ldots,y_n$ are generic solutions of $P_{II}(α_1),\ldots,P_{II}(α_n)$, respectively, and $tr.deg_{\mathbb{C}(t)}\mathbb{C}(t)(y_1,y_1',\ldots,y_n,y_n')<2n$, then for some $i<j$, we have that $α_i\pmα_j\in\mathbb{Z}$, and $y_i=T(y_j)$ for a classical Bäcklund transformation $T$. In particular, the classical Bäcklund transformations are the only Bäcklund transformations in the second Painlevé family.

column6: Dimension drop for superlevel sets of the uniform Littlewood constant
column7: For $(x,y)\in\mathbb{R}^2$ and $Q\ge 1$, set $F_Q(x,y)=Q\min_{1\le q\le Q}\lVert qx\rVert\lVert qy\rVert$, where $q$ ranges over positive integers and $\lVert\cdot\rVert$ denotes distance to the nearest integer. The set on which the uniform Littlewood constant $L=\limsup_{Q\to\infty}F_Q$ is positive has full Hausdorff dimension. We prove that for every fixed $c>0$ the superlevel set $\{L\ge c\}$ has Hausdorff dimension strictly less than two. More precisely, the Lebesgue measure of $\{(x,y)\in[0,1]^2:F_Q(x,y)\ge c\}$ is $O_c(Q^{-κ(c)})$ for some $κ(c)>0$ and all $Q\ge 2$. The proof combines large deviations for one diagonal action on the space of unimodular lattices with effective equidistribution of expanding horospheres for another.

column6: Forbidden subset sums in a linear range: an inverse theorem and the Erdős-Graham irregularity problem
column7: For $c>0$ let $f_c(n)$ be the largest size of a set $A\subseteq\{1,\dots,\lfloor cn\rfloor\}$ such that $n$ is not a sum of distinct elements of $A$. Erdős and Graham asked whether $f_c(n)$ depends on $n$ in an irregular way (Erdős Problem \#361). We prove that $f_c(n)=\lfloor cn\rfloor-\lceil n/2\rceil$ for $c\ge 1$, while for $0<c<1$ the ratio $f_c(n)/n$ has $\limsup$ equal to $c/2$, attained along odd $n$, and, along the integers $n$ whose least non-divisor equals a prime power $q$, tends to \[ \max\Bigl\{\frac cq,\; c-\frac12+\frac{1-c}{q}\Bigr\} \qquad\text{whenever } 2^{q-2}\min\{c,1-c\}\le 1 . \] Consequently $f_c(n)/n$ converges if and only if $c\ge1$; for $0<c<1$ it has at least two limit points, and arbitrarily many as $c\to0^+$ or $c\to1^-$. For $c=1/2$ the set of limit points is exactly $\{1/6,1/4\}$. The upper bounds follow from an inverse theorem of independent interest: if $s\ge1$, $q$ is the least positive integer not dividing $s$, and $\varepsilon>0$, then every $A\subseteq\{1,\dots,E\}$ with $|A|\ge E/q+\varepsilon T$ has a subset summing to $sT$, uniformly for all sufficiently large $T$ and all $E\le sT/2^{q-2}$. For $s=2$, this extends Alon's theorem on subsets of $\{1,\dots,N\}$ with no subset sum equal to $2N$. The results for $c\ge1$ and the $\limsup$, as well as the limits and the inverse theorem for $q\in\{2,3\}$, have been formalized and machine-checked in the Lean~4 proof assistant.

column6: Irregular weight-one Eisenstein series and Euler systems
column7: Let $f=E_1(χ_1,χ_2)$ be an irregular Eisenstein series of weight one, that is, with $χ_1(p)=χ_2(p)$, and consider the generically cuspidal ordinary family passing through it. When $χ_1$, $χ_2$ and $χ_1χ_2^{-1}$ are primitive of the same conductor, we show that the specialization at $f$ of the modular-symbol $p$-adic $L$-function of this family, with periods taken in the cohomology of the compactified modular curves, factors as a product of two Kubota--Leopoldt $p$-adic $L$-functions attached to $χ_1$ and $χ_2$. Since there are no complex critical values in weight one, the factorization is obtained directly from the cohomological construction: we compute the tame-twisted modular measure by means of the localized Sharifi map and explicit reciprocity, and show that tame twisting identifies the compact period modules at weight one. This gives a weight-one analogue of the factorization of Bellaïche--Dasgupta for critical-slope Eisenstein series. As applications, and under explicit specialization hypotheses, we compare Kato classes with circular units, Heegner classes with elliptic units, and diagonal cycles with Kato classes through two successive Eisenstein degenerations. We also discuss the passage from compact to open periods, and include an exposition of the congruence and degeneration methods underlying these comparisons.

column6: The lifting problem for Galois representations of global fields
column7: We prove that all mod $2$ Galois representations of a global field lift modulo $4$. In contrast, for every odd prime $p$, we exhibit examples of global Galois representations modulo $p$ that do not lift modulo $p^2$. Our methods also allow us to prove liftability of generalized quaternion groups and hence to complete the classification of liftable finite groups initiated by Khare and Merkurjev.

column6: Depth-0 supercuspidal L-packets of tame covers
column7: We generalize DeBacker and Reeder's construction (or rather, its refinement by Kaletha) of depth-0 supercuspidal L-packets to tame covers of unramified reductive groups defined by étale levels. These include, in particular, all tame covers associated to Brylinski-Deligne data. We prove that our L-packets satisfy invariance of formal degrees and an appropriate notion of stability.

column5: Christopher J. Eagle; Isaac Goldbring; Timothy H. McNicholl; Russell Miller
column6: Effectively nuclear C*-algebras
column7: We study the computable content of nuclearity for $C^*$-algebras. We show that nuclearity effectivizes automatically: a presentation of a $C^*$-algebra is effectively nuclear, in the sense that the completely positive approximations witnessing nuclearity can be computed uniformly from the data they approximate, if and only if it is a computable presentation of a nuclear $C^*$-algebra, and likewise for the effectivization of the Choi--Effros form of nuclearity. The main tool is an effective version of the Arveson extension theorem: we prove that the $n$-th matrix numerical range of a tuple from a computable presentation is computably compact, uniformly in all of its data, and deduce an algorithm which converts an approximately attainable tuple of matrices into a computable unital completely positive map attaining it. A byproduct is that the computable states of any computable presentation of a unital $C^*$-algebra are weak$^*$-dense in its state space. We also prove that the Cuntz algebras $\mathcal{O}_n$ are computably categorical and obtain an effective form of Kirchberg--Phillips absorption. By contrast with the conditions above, we do not know whether every computable presentation of a nuclear $C^*$-algebra admits a computable embedding into $\mathcal{O}_2$ with a computable conditional expectation; we answer this affirmatively for commutative $C^*$-algebras, for AF algebras, and, by a dynamical argument using invariant states, for the group $C^*$-algebras of a class of amenable groups including all finitely presented residually finite ones. Finally, we show that the set of indices of computable presentations of nuclear $C^*$-algebras is $Π^0_2$, and that the corresponding set for c.e. presentations is $Π^0_2$-hard; the latter rests on a result of independent interest, namely that amenability of computable groups is $Π^0_2$-complete within the class of computable groups.

column6: Forcing global $Π^2_n$ uniformization with or without projective determinacy
column7: We construct a set-forcing extension of $L$ which has the same reals as $L$ and satisfies the $Π^2_n$-uniformization property for every $n\geq1$. Assuming $ω$ Woodin cardinals and a measurable cardinal above them, we also obtain a forcing extension of $L(\mathbb R)^{M_ω}$ which has the same reals and satisfies projective determinacy together with the $Π^2_n$-uniformization property for every $n\geq1$.

column5: Anjelin Mariya Johnson; S. N. Fathima
column6: New Congruences for Simultaneously $l$-Regular and $t$-Distinct Partition in $k$-Colors
column7: Let $RD_{\ell,t}^k(n)$ enumerates the number of $k$-colored simultaneously $l$-regular and $t$-distinct partitions. In this article, we establish some new infinite families of congruences modulo prime $p$, $p\geq5$ and modulo powers of 5 for $RD_{\ell,t}^k(n)$. For instance, for each $n\geq0$, $0\leqα\leq{2k-2}$ and $k\geq1$, \begin{align*} \sum_{n=0}^{\infty}RD_{(5^{2k-1},5^{2k-1})}^2\big(5^{2k+α-1}n+\frac{9\cdot5^{2k+α-1}-2\cdot5^{2k-1}+1}{12}\big)q^n\equiv& 0\pmod{5^{k+\left[\fracα{2}\right]}} \end{align*}

column5: Yongbo Xia; Chunlei Li; Xiangyong Zeng; Tor Helleseth
column6: Correlation distribution for a class of Niho exponents via self-conjugate-reciprocal polynomials and Kloosterman sums
column7: Let $q=2^m$ for an even $m\geq 6$ and let $d=s(q-1)+1$ with $4s\equiv5\pmod{q+1}$. In this paper, the correlation distribution between a binary m-sequence of period $q^2-1$ and its $d$-decimation is considered. The cross-correlation function takes seven values $q(i-1)-1$ for $0\leq i\leq 6$, and we determine their frequencies based on the study of low-degree self-conjugate-reciprocal polynomials and three mixed Kloosterman sums, which are finally expressed in terms of $K_m(1)$ and $K_m(ω)$, where $K_m(\cdot)$ is the Kloomsterman sum on the finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$ and $ω$ is a primitive element of $\mathbb{F}_4$.

column6: Weak Generators in Stable Module Categories
column7: The aim of this note is to show that the existence of weak generators in the stable module category of a ring, or equivalently, of $p$-indigent modules in the terminology of Holston et al., depends on the underlying model of set theory.

column5: Caihua Luo; Xu Song; Yilin Zeng
column6: Commuting pairs in lattices of reductive Lie algebras
column7: We count ordered commuting pairs in a full lattice \(Λ\) in a reductive Lie algebra \(\g\) over \(\Q\). For a fixed convex body \(B\) containing the origin in its interior, the count in \(HB\) is \(C_{Λ,B}H^{\dim\g+\dim Z(\g)}\) with a power-saving error. The leading term comes from pairs whose projections to each simple ideal are linearly dependent over its centroid. Their slopes index an absolutely convergent sum of section volumes for \(C_{Λ,B}\). Subtracting the contribution of dependent pairs from the finite-field Fourier sums gives cancellation at generic dependent frequencies. For independent frequencies, we bound the dimension of the locus where the corresponding hyperplane contains an irreducible component of a nonzero bracket fibre. For \(n\ge3\), the number of ordered commuting pairs in \(M_n(\Z)\) with entries of absolute value at most \(H\) is \[ \frac{2(n+3)ζ(n^2-2)}{(n+1)ζ(n^2-1)} (2\lfloor H\rfloor+1)^{n^2+1} +O_n\!\left(H^{n^2+1-1/(n+1)}\right), \] confirming the exponent \(n^2+1\) predicted by Browning, Sawin and Wang~\cite{BSW}.

column6: The Ulam sequence grows subexponentially
column7: We prove that the $n$-th element of the Ulam sequence, a somewhat mysterious recursively-defined sequence of positive integers, has size $e^{O(\sqrt{n})}$; previous upper bounds were exponential in $n$. Our argument uses an additive-combinatorial lemma, possibly of independent interest, about covering finite difference sets with multiplicatively short intervals. The proofs are due to ChatGPT.

column6: A large ultrafilter number at $\aleph_ω$
column7: Gitik constructed a model where $\aleph_ω$ is strong limit, $2^{\aleph_ω}=\aleph_{ω+2}$ and every strongly uniform ultrafilter on $\aleph_ω$ has character $\aleph_{ω+2}$. We show that in fact every uniform ultrafilter on $\aleph_ω$ has character $\aleph_{ω+2}$ in that model.

column6: Semistable 1-Motives: Monodromy, Explicit Periods, and Local Duality
column7: Let $K/\mathbf Q_p$ be unramified, with $p>2$. For a $1$-motive with constant lattice, split torus, and good abelian quotient, we compute the semistable extension complex from toric valuations and formal-group logarithms. A canonical monodromy boundary exists for every semistable representation; it detects splitting over crystalline periods and the increase in monodromy rank. For the stated $1$-motives, this boundary and the unramified quotient recover the restricted local Tate pairing, with exponential radicals. Nonsplit elliptic examples, Raynaud uniformization, and a height-one positive-period bound explain the geometric range. For toric motives we construct actual periods, convergent Robba bases, and integral action matrices. A toric basis family has perfect projective/trace-zero matrix duality, including its exact integral defect. An explicit residue-zero solution operator constructs every dual Herr class. Applied componentwise, the same operator gives relative full dual lifts for general constant-lattice $1$-motives once their coefficient sequence is specified. Finally, finite-base coefficient traces realize division-tower Iwasawa cohomology for any Tate lattice, and the period cup pairing equals the arithmetic group-ring pairing.

column5: Heiko Knospe; Jiahe Shen; Roger Van Peski
column6: Refined random matrix conjectures for zeros of $p$-adic $L$-functions
column7: We make and test the conjecture that for $p$-adic $L$-functions associated to quadratic Dirichlet characters and their Teichmüller twists, all local statistics of zeros in the unit disk match those of $p$-adic random matrix eigenvalues. This generalizes the case of the number of zeros in the unit disk previously conjectured by Ellenberg-Jain-Venkatesh, which was well-supported by numerics, as well as the case of the discriminant, where their numerics were more ambiguous. Using recent random matrix results on local statistics of eigenvalues, we make the random matrix prediction explicit for many statistics, analogous to local densities and pair-correlations in the complex setting. To test these, we compute data on $p$-adic $L$-functions for characters of conductor up to $10^7$, and for certain statistics in windows above $10^{10}$. We find good agreement with the new random matrix predictions for these statistics, as well as for the discriminant.

column5: Tim Browning; Stephanie Chan; Nick Rome
column6: Rational lines on pairs of quadrics and cubic hypersurfaces
column7: We study rational lines on smooth intersections of two quadrics and on smooth cubic hypersurfaces over number fields. For an intersection of two quadrics in $n$ variables, we prove the Hasse principle and weak approximation for the variety of lines when $n\geq 11$, and more generally for the variety of $r$-planes when $n\geq 3r+8$. In this range an $r$-plane exists over the ground field if and only if one exists over every real completion. For the variety of lines, we also prove the Hasse principle and weak approximation when $n\geq 8$, conditional on the finiteness of certain Tate-Shafarevich groups. For a smooth cubic hypersurface in $n$ variables, we prove that a line exists over the ground field when $n\geq 23$.

column6: Extreme central $L$-values of almost prime quadratic twists of elliptic curves II
column7: We prove lower bounds for central $L$-values of quadratic twists of an elliptic curve by discriminants with at most five prime factors. Under the rank-zero Birch--Swinnerton-Dyer formula, these bounds give large Tate--Shafarevich groups.

column6: HOL in HOL: mechanized soundness, completeness and consistency, with and without infinity
column7: What can a logic certify about a copy of itself? For Church's simple theory of types, formalized as a deep embedding in Isabelle/HOL with Henkin semantics and a natural-deduction calculus, the answer has two tiers. On the first tier, plain Isabelle/HOL certifies the logic without an axiom of infinity, by a standard model with one individual. On the second tier, the logic with a Dedekind-style axiom of infinity is certified only in Isabelle/HOL extended by a large enough set-theoretic universe. Both tiers appear in Harrison's self-verification of HOL Light. What the present formalization adds is Henkin completeness, and with it a semantics that matches the calculus exactly, compactness and model existence on the first tier, and the boundary between the tiers. Comparing two ways of adding infinity to the object logic shows where the boundary lies. One is an infinite domain of individuals, expressed by the first-order sentences "there are at least $n$ individuals", each of which has a finite model; the other is the Dedekind axiom, a single sentence with no finite model, and there the first tier ends. In the calculus the axiom is strictly stronger than the sentences together: it derives each of them, but they do not derive it. The witness is a countable Henkin model in which every sentence holds and the axiom fails, because its function domain is too sparse for an injective, non-surjective self-map. On the second tier, the universe serves one purpose only: to prove the Dedekind axiom consistent. Everything that follows, completeness and even the countable Henkin model of the axiom, is obtained in plain Isabelle/HOL. The universe axiom is Harrison-style, realized in Paulson's ZFC_in_HOL with the domain of every type in $V_{ω+ω}$; with it, full classical higher-order logic with infinity and relational choice is consistent relative to set theory.

column6: Non-vanishing of central $\rm GL_3$ L-values in the level aspect
column7: We study non-vanishing of central standard $L$-values of spherical cuspidal $\mathrm{GL}_3$ newforms of prime level. A logarithmic Möbius mollifier with finite inverse Euler factors, combined with a conjugate term from the functional equation, gives a non-vanishing harmonic proportion of at least $1/2-\varepsilon$ for every $\varepsilon>0$ and all sufficiently large prime levels. The required mixed moment is evaluated by an asymmetric approximate functional equation.

column6: Common values of linear recurrences related to Ankeny-Brauer-Chowla polynomials
column7: Let $P_u(X)=XQ(X)(X-u)+1$, where $Q(X)\in \mathbb{Z}[X]$ is monic, separabel, has constant term $\pm 1$, and degree $q\ge 1$. Denote $(A_n(u))$ the linear recursive sequence having characteristic polynomial $P_u(X)$ and initial terms $A_0,\ldots,A_{q+1}\in \mathbb{Z}$ such that at least one of them is non-zero. Then there exist effectively computable constants $n_0,u_0$ depending only on $Q(X)$ and $\max\{|A_0|,\ldots, |A_{q+1}|\}$ such that if $|A_n(u)| = |A_m(u)|$ holds for some integers $u,n,m$ with $u>u_0$ and $n\not=m$ then $\max\{

column6: Lower bounds on ranks of universal quadratic forms through geometry-of-numbers
column7: We obtain lower bounds for the ranks of universal forms over totally real cubic fields using techniques from geometry-of-numbers and the parametrisation of cubic rings by binary cubics due to Delone--Faddeev. Additionally, our methods give lower bounds for totally real primitive fields of any degree with codifferent generated by a totally positive element.

column5: Dianthe Basak; Matteo Casarosa; Chris Lambie-Hanson; Pedro Marun; Boban Velickovic; Alessandro Vignati
column6: Higher derived limits, Kurepa families and Chang's Conjecture
column7: We investigate the interplay between homological algebra and combinatorial set theory, specifically focusing on the (non)vanishing of higher derived limits of certain inverse systems of abelian groups, denoted $\mathbf C_{[κ]^λ}$, indexed by the ordered sets $([κ]^λ,\subseteq)$, where $λ< κ$ are infinite cardinals. Our first main result is a general structural theorem which provides a generalisation of Goblot's theorem to the setting of locally small directed sets. We then present the first systematic study of generalised cofinal Kurepa families. We establish their existence in the constructible universe $L$ and under specific cardinal arithmetic hypotheses. Then, we apply our structural result to show that $\mathrm{lim}^{n+2} \mathbf{C}_{[κ]^{\aleph_n}} = 0$ in environments where the appropriate cofinal Kurepa families exist. In contrast, we explore conditions that force these derived limits to be nonzero. In particular, we prove that certain instances of Chang's conjecture (CC), together with the existence of suitable $\diamondsuit$ sequences, imply that $\mathrm{lim}^{n+2} \mathbf{C}_{[κ]^{\aleph_n}} \neq 0$ for appropriate values of $κ$. Adapting forcing techniques from Eskew and Hayut, we construct models of these instances of CC together with the required $\diamondsuit$ sequences, establishing the consistency, for each $n \in \mathbb{N}$, of $\mathrm{lim}^{n+2} \mathbf{C}_{[\aleph_{ω_n}]^{\aleph_n}} \neq 0$.

column6: Long rational and Gaussian integer multiplication
column7: Long integer multiplication is a fundamental operation in computational algebra, heavily relying on Toom--Cook and related evaluation-interpolation algorithms. Conventional wisdom dictates that multiplication on the Gaussian integers $\mathbb{Z}[i]$ is reduced to standard rational integer multiplication, since $\mathbb{Z}[i]$ is a ring extension of $\mathbb{Z}$. We show that this approach is far from optimal and moreover inverting this established paradigm, that is reducing rational to Gaussian multiplication, leads to faster rational integer multiplication algorithms. We introduce a novel Toom--Cook framework that reduces rational long integer multiplication to Gaussian integer multiplication, yielding a strictly more efficient computational pipeline. By taking advantage of the special properties of the rational integer domain inside the Gaussian integers, we achieve a more favourable algebraic structure that reduces the overall arithmetic cost in every metric. To validate this theoretical shift, we provide a complete implementation of our algorithm. Benchmarks demonstrate that our approach outperforms the highly optimised GNU Multiple Precision Arithmetic Library (GMP) by up to 29\%, bridging a fundamental theoretical insight with significant practical improvements in high-performance computer algebra.

column6: The minimal excludant of $\ell$-regular overpartitions
column7: Andrews and Newman \cite{AN1} introduced the minimal excludant (mex) of an integer partition, and Aricheta and Donato \cite{AD} extended it to overpartitions. More recently, Meher \cite{Meher} and Tejash, Bhowmick and Meher \cite{TBM} studied the analogous statistic for $\ell$-regular partitions. In this article, for an integer $\ell\ge 2$, we define the minimal excludant $\omex_\ell(π)$ of an $\ell$-regular overpartition $π$ as the smallest positive integer that is not divisible by $\ell$ and does not occur as a non-overlined part of $π$. We study $\sm{\ell}(n)$, the sum of $\omex_\ell(π)$ over all $\ell$-regular overpartitions $π$ of $n$. We obtain generating functions for $\sm{\ell}(n)$ as eta-quotients for $\ell=2$ and $\ell=3$. Later, motivated from \cite{TBM}, we obtained explicit generating functions for $\sm{\ell}(n)$. We show that $\sm{\ell}(n)$ is weakly increasing in $n$, and we derive Hardy--Ramanujan type asymptotic formulas for $\sm{2}(n)$ and $\sm{3}(n)$. We then determine the parity of both functions completely: $\sm{2}(n)$ is even for every $n\ge 1$, while $\sm{3}(n)$ is odd if and only if $n=0$ or $n$ is a centred hexagonal number. Also, we obtain for every $\ell\ge3$, $\sm{\ell}(n)$ is odd for infinitely many $n$, and the number of such $n\le X$ is $\gg\sqrt{X}$. Finally, we establish congruences for these functions modulo $3$, $4$ and $8$.

column6: Equidistribution of Gross lattices of supersingular elliptic curves
column7: For a prime $p$, we consider two important families of integral quadratic lattices associated to isomorphism classes of supersingular elliptic curves over $\overline{\mathbb{F}_{p}}$, the lattices of endomorphisms of trace zero, and the Gross lattices of endomorphisms. We prove effective equidistribution of the shapes of these lattices as $p\to\infty$ through primes, in the arithmetic locally symmetric space of unimodular lattices up to isometry. As an application, we obtain, as $p\to\infty$, the asymptotic distribution of successive minima of these lattices. These results are proved using tools from homogeneous dynamics, in particular, the key dynamical input is a recent adelic equidistribution theorem due to Einsiedler, Margulis, Mohammadi, and Venkatesh.

column6: The Möbius function of factorizations with a simple prime factor
column7: The poset of factorizations of a positive integer $n$ (ordered by refinement) is known to have a very irregular Möbius function. We prove that this function becomes completely explicit whenever $n$ is divisible by a prime $q$ to the first power only ($q^2 \nmid n$). Specifically, between a factorization with $k$ factors and $n$ itself, the Möbius function is given by $(-1)^{k-1}$ multiplied by the number of ways to order the factors that are not divisible by $q$. As a consequence, the sum of the absolute values of the Möbius function over this interval equals twice the number of ordered factorizations of $n/q$.

column6: The Chabauty--Kim dimension inequality via noncommutative Iwasawa theory
column7: We establish Kim's conjectural dimension inequality for smooth projective geometrically connected curves $C/\mathbb{Q}$ of genus at least two with a rational basepoint. For every odd prime $p$ of good reduction, we prove that $$\mathrm{dim} H_f^1(G_{\mathbb{Q},Σ},U_n^\mathrm{ét}) < \mathrm{dim}(U_n^{\mathrm{dR}}/F^0)$$ for all sufficiently large $n$, where $U_n^\mathrm{ét}$ and $U_n^\mathrm{dR}$ are the $n$'th lower central series truncations of the $\mathbb{Q}_p$-pro-unipotent geometric étale, and de Rham fundamental groups of $C$, and $Σ$ is any finite set of places containing $p$, $\infty$, and the primes of bad reduction. Inspired by Coates and Kim's work on curves with CM Jacobians, we use noncommutative Iwasawa theory to bound second Galois cohomology through dimensions of kernels of certain Iwasawa operators, acting on finite dimensional representations of the ambient generalized symplectic group. We establish bounds for these kernels in terms of the highest weight and dimension of the ambient symplectic representation. No restriction is imposed on the Jacobian's geometric endomorphism ring or its Tate-module Galois image. Consequently, the Chabauty--Kim loci are finite at all sufficiently large levels, recovering the Mordell theorem over $\mathbb{Q}$ through the Chabauty--Kim method.

column6: Short quadratic exponential sums with primes in major arcs
column7: Using the second moment of Dirichlet $L$-functions on the critical line over the major arcs ${\mathfrak M}({\mathscr L}^b)$, with $τ=y^3x^{-1}{\mathscr L}^{-b_1}$, and excluding a small neighborhood of the centers of these arcs, i.e., those $α$ satisfying $|α-\frac{a}{q}|>(8πy^2)^{-1}$, for $y\ge x^{1-\frac{\scriptstyle1}{\scriptstyle{9-4\sqrt{2}}}}{\mathscr L}^{c_2}$, where $c_2=\frac{2A+24+(\sqrt{2}-1)b_1}{2\sqrt{2}-1}$, we obtain the estimate $$ S_2(α;x,y)=\sum_{x-y<n\le x}Λ(n)e(αn^2)\ll y\,{\mathscr L}^{-A}. $$ Moreover, in a small neighborhood of the center of the major arcs, defined by $|α-\frac{a}{q}|\le(8πy^2)^{-1}$, for $y\ge x^{\frac{\scriptstyle5}{\scriptstyle8}}{\mathscr L}^{1,5A+0,25b+18}$, an asymptotic formula with a remainder term is obtained for $S_2(α;x,y)$, where $A$, $b_1$, and $b$ are arbitrary fixed positive constants, and ${\mathscr L}=\ln xq$.

column6: Arithmetical and set-theoretic semantics of the logic of problems and propositions
column7: Kolmogorov interpreted intuitionistic logic as a calculus of problems and later remarked that a complete treatment should deal with problems and propositions together. Melikhov's logic HC is such a joint two-sorted system: it combines classical propositions with intuitionistic problems by means of two modalities, the problem !A (``find a proof of the proposition A'') and the proposition phi (``the problem phi has a solution''). We give the language of HC a formal semantics in which the modalities are read literally: solutions of !A are proofs of A in a fixed formal theory, ?phi states that phi has a solution, and the connectives on problems are interpreted as in Kleene realizability. Three variants are studied: the arithmetical semantics I (provability in PA), its external version E (truth in the standard model), and the set-theoretic semantics B over ZF, where problem variables are ``black boxes'' and a quantifier Pi over them is available. Validity is defined as the existence of a computable uniform solution. We determine which schemes are valid, build calculi HCI, HCE, HCB sound with respect to the three semantics, and derive Lob's scheme from the fixed-point lemma inside the common core of our calculi and HC. The propositional fragments of HCI and HCE are exactly the provability logics GL and GLS; the positive modality-free fragment of valid problems is intuitionistic logic, while the full modality-free fragment lies strictly above it (Rose's formula is valid, Scott's principle is not). We compare the calculi with HC, which turns out to be incompatible with fixed points, prove independence results and list open questions.

column5: Souad El Otmani; Musbahu Idris; Jean-Marc Sac-Epee
column6: On Borwein polynomials with multiple roots outside the unit disk
column7: A Borwein polynomial has coefficients in ${-1,0,1}$ and nonzero constant and leading coefficients. We seek Borwein polynomials having a multiple root outside the unit disk. To this end, we consider the powers $L^2$ and $L^3$ of Lehmer's polynomial $L$, which has a real root $τ>1$. Since $L$ has exceptionally small Mahler measure, the theorem of Bombieri and Vaaler guarantees the existence of Borwein multiples of these powers. Such multiples have $τ$ as a root of multiplicity at least 2 and 3, respectively. Mossinghoff (2003, Algorithm 3, p. 323) constructed examples that, under the substitution $x\mapsto -x$, yield such multiples. The main contribution of this paper is to determine the least possible degrees of Borwein multiples of $L^2$ and $L^3$, with and without symmetry restrictions on their coefficients, and to describe their degree spectra. For $L^2$, the minimum degree is 34 without symmetry restrictions, 38 among self-reciprocal multiples, and 41 among antireciprocal multiples. For $L^3$, the corresponding minimum degrees are 115, 115, and 117. We determine the complete degree spectra for $L^2$ and, for $L^3$, classify the degrees from 115 to 150 for which self-reciprocal or antireciprocal Borwein multiples exist, giving an explicit example for each admissible degree in each symmetry class. Further constructions yield Borwein multiples of $L^3$ in every degree $D\geq 215$, with both symmetry types for every $D\geq 231$.

column6: Matrix ultraproducts have trivial fundamental group
column7: We prove that every tracial ultraproduct $\prod_{\mathcal{U}} M_n(\mathbb{C})$ of matrix algebras has trivial fundamental group. In particular, this establishes that there are uncountably many nonisomorphic matrix ultraproducts, answering a question of Sorin Popa. We actually prove the stronger result that every matrix ultraproduct has trivial first-order fundamental group and thus our techniques are model-theoretic in nature.

column6: The $\operatorname{Proj}$ construction for pro-graded Huber pairs
