As an application, we give an explicit description of the category of isocrystals over a finite field.

column6: Congruence Patterns in Spectral Gaps of mod $p$ Markoff Graphs
column7: We establish lower bounds on the second-largest eigenvalue of mod $p$ Markoff graphs for three infinite, positive-density families of primes $p$, each defined by congruence conditions. These lower bounds arise from the structure of integral orbits on Markoff-type surfaces over certain number fields, and are strong enough to establish that $$\liminf_{\substack{p\rightarrow\infty\\p\equiv1\pmod{4}}}λ_2(\Mar^*(\F_p)) > 2.875> 2\sqrt{2},$$ partially proving a conjecture of de Courcy-Ireland and Lee, and that $$\limsup_{\substack{p\rightarrow\infty\\p\equiv 3\pmod{4}}}(λ_2(\Mar^*(\F_p)) > 2.835 > 2\sqrt{2},$$ disproving another conjecture of the same.

column6: On the V-toothpick sequence
column7: We give a generating function for the V-toothpick sequence and an algorithm that computes any term in time polynomial in the number of binary digits of its index. We determine its quadratic growth and periodic fluctuations, and give convergent series for the constants in its asymptotic bounds.

column6: Multifractal analysis of Takagi-type functions built from beta-expansion cylinders
column7: We study a family of Takagi functions obtained by placing a normalized tent on each beta-expansion cylinder, with amplitude $β^{-αn}$ at order $n$, where $β>1$ and $0<α\le1$. We characterize their pointwise Hölder regularity in terms of cylinder lengths and distances from the point under consideration. The characterization holds more generally for nested interval partitions with exponentially decreasing mesh, without requiring interval lengths at a given order to be comparable. For beta-expansion cylinders, we compute the full multifractal spectrum whenever the remainders of the expansion of $1$ have a finite upper exponential decay rate. The functions are monofractal when this rate vanishes, as it does for Parry, Pisot and Salem bases. When it is positive, the spectrum is affine on a nondegenerate interval. The bases defined by $\sum_{k\ge0}β_\ell^{-\ell^k}=1$, for integers $\ell\ge2$, give explicit non-monofractal examples. We also prove that every function in the family is nowhere differentiable.

column6: On the $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear relations among multiple zeta values in positive characteristic
column7: This paper gives a new path to determine all $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear relations among multiple zeta values in positive characteristic, which had been done by Huang, Lai, Li and the author. The path used in this paper is based on the idea of operator generation, which originated from the work of Todd, developed by the author, and independently by Im-Kim-Ngo Dac.

column6: On counting integer symmetric matrices of fixed determinant in families of slant boxes
column7: In this article, we develop an upper bound for the number of integral symmetric matrices of fixed determinant in a slant box with coefficients bounded by some given power of the volume of the slant box. We develop a counting method that expands on Shankar-Siad-Swaminathan's work on rank-3 integer symmetric matrices of fixed determinant to higher-rank matrices using geometry-of-numbers methods and invariant theory on the splitting of quadratic forms associated with the determinant formula into corresponding linear forms. We expect this generalization will allow us to apply the counting results to arithmetic statistics frameworks. In forthcoming work, we will apply the counting results to study the distribution of 2-torsion subgroups of class groups of unit-monogenised number fields.

column6: Narrower arithmetic progressions in the primes
column7: For each fixed $k\geq 3$ and $δ> 0$, we prove that every subset of the primes up to $X$ of relative density at least $δ$ contains a non-trivial $k$-term arithmetic progression with common difference $O_{k,δ,\varepsilon}((\log X)^{k\cdot 2^{k-3}+\varepsilon})$, for any $\varepsilon>0$. This improves the previous exponent $(k-1)2^{k-2}$. The main ingredient is a relative Szemerédi theorem for narrow progressions under weaker linear forms conditions.

column5: Michael Bersudsky; Seongmin Kim; Seonhee Lim
column6: Irreducible $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{R})$-action on projective $k$-lattices and Frobenius numbers
column7: The irreducible representation of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ induces an action on the space $X_k(\mathbb{R}^n)$ of projective classes of rank $k$-discrete subgroups in $\mathbb{R}^n$. For every lattice subgroup of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ and every starting point in $X_k(\mathbb{R}^n)$ and $2\leq k<n$, we prove convergence of the orbit averages over expanding norm balls and give a complete, explicit description of their limits. In an overview, every limit is supported on the subbundle over the unique compact $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{R})$-orbit in the Grassmannian. The conditional measures on the fibers are either uniform on finite sets or convex combinations of at most two homogeneous measures associated with split simple subgroups of $\mathrm{PGL}_k(\mathbb{R})$ containing the principal $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{R})$. Another objective of our work is to relate weak-$*$ limits of probability measures on $X_{n-1}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ supported on the projective classes of lattices orthogonal to integer vectors with limiting distributions of the corresponding normalized Frobenius numbers. This correspondence gives limit laws for vectors sampled from certain proper subvarieties, extending J. Marklof's work on sampling from full-dimensional domains. Specifically, together with our results for $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ orbits in $X_{n-1}(\mathbb{R}^n)$, this correspondence gives limit laws for primitive integer vectors sampled from $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{R})$-orbits. Using an earlier result of the first author and Shapira, we obtain analogous laws for integer vectors sampled on level sets of certain quadratic forms, as the level tends to infinity.

column6: Irreducible components of affine Deligne-Lusztig variety in the affine flag variety
column7: We establish a bijection between elements of stable Demazure crystals and labeled longest increasing paths in the double Bruhat graph. As an application, we show that the orbits of irreducible components of certain special affine Deligne-Lusztig varieties (ADLVs) in the affine flag variety of a split reductive group are counted by weight multiplicities of the associated Demazure modules for the dual group. By decomposing an arbitrary ADLV into strata that are iterated fibrations over these special ADLVs, we then obtain a formula for the number of orbits of irreducible components for ADLVs in the affine flag variety, generalizing the numerical form of the Chen-Zhu conjecture.

column6: Superspecial curves of genus two over prime fields: Frobenius types and rational (2,2)-kernels
column7: Superspecial curves of genus two over a prime field $\mathbb{F}_p$, and the rational $(2,2)$-isogenies between their Jacobians, are the vertices and edges of the graph on which genus-two isogeny-based cryptography is built. Let $C$ be such a curve, with Jacobian $J$ and Frobenius endomorphism $π$. We show that $π^2 = p\,α_*$ for a unique automorphism $α$ of $C$ over $\mathbb{F}_p$ whose action on the Weierstrass points is the square of that of Frobenius. For $p \ge 7$ this gives the list of Frobenius types of the Weierstrass points: eight types, each with its Weil polynomial, a congruence condition on $p$, and its number 15, 3, 3, 7, 1, 1, 3 or 1 of $\mathbb{F}_p$-rational $(2,2)$-kernels; when all Weierstrass points are rational, the 2-Tate pairing on $J[2]$ is determined by $p \bmod 8$. We then prove closed formulas, in terms of class numbers of imaginary quadratic orders and of $ζ_{\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt p)}(-1)$, for the mass of the curves of each type and for the mass of the rational kernels whose quotient is a product of elliptic curves. For $π^2 = \pm p$ the total masses are due to Ibukiyama and to Xue and Yu; our proofs use the 2-adic Tate modules, the symmetry of the Richelot correspondence and Eichler's mass formula, and, for the other curves, modules over orders of a quartic CM field. The kernels are counted through gluings of supersingular elliptic curves. As a consequence, the proportion of rational kernels with decomposed quotient is of order $p^{-1/2}(1+L(1,χ))$, where $χ$ is the quadratic character of $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-p})$. All formulas agree with an exact enumeration for the 37 primes $7 \le p \le 173$. Finally we describe the graph of $\mathbb{F}_p$-rational Richelot isogenies, which is far from connected in the range computed, and discuss what these results say about its use in isogeny-based cryptography.

column5: Diego A. Mejía; Ulises Ariet Ramos-García
column6: Preserving Ramsey ultrafilters with tree forcings
column7: We define a wide class of tree forcings that we call $\textit{normed-tree forcings}$ and prove that they can preserve Ramsey ultrafilters. These include $\textit{fat-tree forcings}$ as particular cases. As an application, we prove the consistency with $\mathsf{ZFC}$ of $\mathfrak{d}=\mathfrak{u}=\aleph_1 < \mathsf{minLc}=\mathfrak{c}=\aleph_2$, where $\mathfrak{d}$ denotes the dominating number, $\mathfrak{u}$ the ultrafilter number, and $\mathsf{minLc}$ the minimum localization cardinal. This solves some open questions about pairs of classical cardinal characteristics, such as the consistency of both $\mathfrak{e}_{\mathsf{ubd}}$ and its dual strictly larger than $\mathfrak{u}$.

column6: Optimal homological stability: bounding secondary terms of Cohen-Lenstra moments and $S_d$-fields over $\mathbb{F}_q[t]$
column7: We prove an explicit stability line for the homology $H_i(\mathrm{Hur}_n^c,\mathbb{Q})$ of any Hurwitz space associated to a finite rack $c$ depending only on its homology up to some finite $n$. Moreover, as the range of $n$ increases, the slope of the resulting stability line converges to the optimal slope. Thus, for any Hurwitz space, a finite computation will yield near-optimal bounds on secondary terms for the corresponding arithmetic statistics problem. Our theorem also applies more generally to higher order stability, Frobenius weights, and braided vector spaces. As a special case of our theorem, we can deduce stability lines depending only on when $H_0(\mathrm{Hur}^c_n,\mathbb{Q})$ stabilizes, which are sharp in some cases. We apply this to two families of Hurwitz spaces to obtain bounds on the secondary term for (1) the number of $S_d$-degree $d$ function fields with squarefree discriminant, and (2) Cohen-Lenstra moments.

column6: Heights and energies of polarized fibrations of varieties
column7: Let $X\to C$ be a projective fibration over a curve over a global field. We prove a height inequality for relatively nef adelic line bundles on $X$ whose underlying line bundles are nef. For a nef, relatively ample line bundle over a finitely generated field, we deduce a lower bound for the local energy at almost every complex or nonarchimedean realization of a fixed polarized model. Over $\mathbb C$, for an ample line bundle and a smooth positive polarization, the Euler--Lagrange equation is the Calabi--Yau equation. On the projective bundle of a vector bundle of degree zero, our energy on quotient metrics agrees with Donaldson's functional when the determinant metric is fixed. We propose a construction of canonical heights on parameter spaces using envelopes of local energies.

column5: Zhenghui Li; Benchao Su; Zhixiang Wu
column6: Bernstein-Zelevinsky duality for equivariant vector bundles on Drinfeld spaces
column7: We study duality and finiteness of locally analytic representations arising from compactly supported coherent cohomology of Drinfeld spaces. We prove that Grothendieck--Serre duality for equivariant vector bundles realizes Bernstein--Zelevinsky duality of locally analytic representations. We follow the strategy of Fargues for $\ell$-adic sheaves and obtain resolutions of locally analytic representations by compactly induced representations. The resolutions motivate us to introduce the notion of locally analytic representations of compact presentation, which generalizes the notion of finitely presented representations. These representations are related to prim objects on the classifying stack in the sense of $6$-functor formalism and their extension groups to admissible locally analytic representations are finite-dimensional. As an application, we establish Serre duality for extension groups of locally analytic representations of $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{Q}_p)$ attached to non-trianguline de Rham Galois representations under the $p$-adic local Langlands correspondence.

column5: Vinicius de Oliveira Rodrigues; Fabrício Yohei Ynone
column6: Pseudocompact MAD families under $\mathfrak b=\mathfrak c$
column7: We prove that if the bounding number $\mathfrak b$ equals the cardinality of the continuum $\mathfrak c$, then every infinite almost disjoint family of size less than $\mathfrak c$ can be extended to a maximal almost disjoint family whose Isbell--Mrówka space has a pseudocompact Vietoris hyperspace.

column6: Zero-sum subsequences of cross number $1$ over cyclic groups
column7: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group, and let $\mathsf{T}(G)$ be the smallest integer $t$ such that every sequence of length $t$ over $G$ contains a nonempty zero-sum subsequence of cross number $1$. We determine the exact value of $\mathsf{T}(C_n)$ for every positive integer $n$, showing that $\mathsf{T}(C_n)=2n-1$ when $n$ is odd and $\mathsf{T}(C_n)=3n/2-1$ when $n$ is even. In particular, $\mathsf{T}(C_n)=\mathsf{s}(C_n)$ for odd $n$.

column6: Generalizing the Gaster--Loustau Theorem via Generalized Discrete Markov Spectra
column7: We realize generalized Markov numbers (GM numbers) for arbitrary $k_1,k_2,k_3\in \mathbb Z_{\ge0}$ as $λ$-lengths of return arcs on a hyperbolic orbifold constructed from local monodromy matrices. The McShane identity of Tan--Wong--Zhang on this orbifold yields a summation identity with multiplicities for the gaps between the associated Markov--Lagrange constants and their limiting value, together with a summation inequality that counts each distinct value once. These results extend the summation identity and inequality of Gaster and Loustau to generalized Markov numbers.

column6: Incidence methods for algebraic expanders over arbitrary fields
column7: Let $A\subset F$ be finite, $N=|A|$, $p=\operatorname{char}F$ (with $p=\infty$ in characteristic zero), and $L=1+\log(2N)$. In the range $N\le p^{1/2}$, we establish \[ |AA+A|\gg N^{129/85}L^{-72/85}. \] This improves the long-standing $3/2$-exponent bound for $AA+A$ in positive characteristic in the range $N\le p^{1/2}$, without any assumption on the multiplicative doubling of $A$. We further establish uniform expansion bounds with exponents $129/85$ and $32/21$ for four families of three-variable product--quotient expanders, together with refined estimates over prime fields. For $λ\in F^\times$ and $N\le p^{1/2}$, our four-variable bounds include \[ |AA+λAA|\gg N^{214/135}L^{-7/9},\qquad |AA-AA|\gg_\varepsilon N^{6681/4175-\varepsilon} \quad(\varepsilon>0). \] In particular, several three- and four-variable targets admit uniform lower bounds with exponents greater than $3/2$ in the large-characteristic range. We also prove bounds with exponent $49/38$ for shifted products and shifted quotients, and for quadratic-image sumsets when $\operatorname{char}F\ne 2$, as well as characteristic-sensitive estimates for $AA+λA/A$ and $(A-A)^\times/(A-A)^\times$. The proofs combine higher-energy inequalities, regularisation, and point--line incidences.

column6: On p-adic asymptotic formulas for slope factors of L-functions of toric exponential sums
column7: Adolphson and Sperber expressed the unique unit root of the $L$-function of a toric exponential sum in terms of $A$-hypergeometric functions, whereas reciprocal zeros and poles of positive slope remain much less understood.We study complete rational factors of arbitrary prescribed slope in families satisfying a chain-level ordinary condition. Our main tool is a new contraction map arising from a twisted block LU factorization of the Frobenius matrix of a nuclear $σ$-module. Its fixed point produces an upper triangularization and the associated slope filtration, while explicit Schur-complement quotients of finite Frobenius iterates approximate the diagonal slope blocks with geometrically decreasing error. At a periodic fiber, successive cancellation in an ordered product of these approximations yields a quotient formed from two finite Frobenius iterates, and the characteristic polynomial of this quotient converges to the complete slope polynomial. Combined with the relative Dwork trace formula, this yields uniform $p$-adic asymptotic formulas for the complete slope factors of the $L$-functions of toric exponential sums. When the relevant slope blocks have rank one, the Schur complements reduce to ratios of leading principal minors and give asymptotic formulas for the individual reciprocal zeros and poles after cancellation.

column6: The Borel Ruziewicz problem
column7: We prove that for $n\ge2$ the normalized surface measure is the only rotation-invariant finitely additive probability measure on the Borel subsets of $\mathbb S^n$, and that for $d\ge3$ Lebesgue measure is the only finitely additive measure on the bounded Borel subsets of $\mathbb{R}^d$ which is invariant under orientation-preserving isometries and normalized on the unit cube. This answers the Borel version of the Ruziewicz problem. On $\mathbb S^n$ it suffices to assume invariance under a finite set of rotations with a spectral gap, and on $\mathbb{R}^d$ under two such sets of rotations about two distinct centres. The main step is a criterion for invariant finitely additive probability measures to vanish on null sets. For a finite nonempty symmetric set of homeomorphisms of a $σ$-compact metrizable space with a quasi-invariant Borel measure $m$ which is finite on compact sets, such as Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb{R}^d$, every invariant finitely additive probability measure on Borel sets vanishes on $m$-null sets if and only if there is $δ>0$ such that every countably additive Borel probability measure supported on an $m$-null Borel set is moved by some generator by at least $δ$ in total variation. Sufficiency is proved by constructing, for every invariant null Borel set, a bounded Borel field on the orbit graph, supported on the set and with divergence at least one there.

column6: The inverse Littlewood problem for multiplicative functions
column7: We formulate and solve the asymptotic inverse Littlewood problem in the class of multiplicative functions. That is, let $f:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{U}\cup\{0\}$ be a bounded completely multiplicative function satisfying $\sum_{p:f(p)=0}1/p<\infty$. We show that \[ \int_0^1 \left|\sum_{n\le x}f(n)e(αn)\right|\,dα\ll\log x \] for all $x\ge3$ if and only if $f(n)=χ(n)n^{it}$ for some Dirichlet character $χ$ and some $t\in\mathbb{R}$.\\ More generally, we show that there is $\varepsilon_0>0$, depending only on the $\ell^2$-density of $f$ (that is, on $\prod_{p:f(p)=0}(1-1/p)$), such that under the weaker hypothesis \[ \int_0^1 \left|\sum_{n\le x}f(n)e(αn)\right|\,dα \ll x^{\varepsilon_0} \] for all $x\ge3$, there are a Dirichlet character $χ$ and $t\in\mathbb{R}$ such that \[ \sum_p\frac{\left|f(p)-χ(p)p^{it}\right|}{p}<\infty. \] We give evidence for the sharpness of such classification, by constructing non-pretentious examples with $L^1$ norm $o(\sqrt{x})$ at every sufficiently large scale, but with ``wild" behavior at the intermediate scales.

column5: Minjia Shi; Mengru Yang; Patrick Solé
column6: Cyclic Self-Dual Codes over Prime-Square Rings and Unimodular Lattices
column7: We present an explicit construction of cyclic Euclidean self-dual codes over $\mathbb{Z}/p^{2}\mathbb{Z}$, where $p$ is an odd prime, and use Construction~A to obtain unimodular lattices with large minimum norms. The construction is based on reciprocal factorizations of $x^n-1$. We explicitly describe the associated residue and torsion codes and analyze the relationship between minimum Euclidean weights and lattice minimum norms. We construct a unimodular lattice of minimum norm~$4$ in dimension~$49$, unimodular lattices of minimum norm~$5$ in dimensions $53$, $55$, $58$, $59$, and~$61$, and extremal unimodular lattices of minimum norm~$6$ in dimensions $69$ and~$71$. Using shadow theory and harmonic theta series, we prove that extremal unimodular lattices do not exist in dimensions $59$ and~$61$. Together with the known upper bounds, these results establish the optimality of the constructed lattices in all eight dimensions. In particular, we determine the previously unknown optimal minimum norms of unimodular lattices in five dimensions: $53$, $55$, $61$, $69$, and~$71$. We further construct unimodular lattices whose minimum norms are exactly one below the corresponding extremal bounds in dimensions $62$, $63$, $65$, $67$, $70$, $89$, $91$, $92$, $93$, and~$94$.

column5: Helga Boyer von Berghof; Daniel C. Mayer
column6: 44 Tropen by Josef Matthias Hauer as orbits under the group of interval shifts
column7: We generate a splitting of the 924 monotonically ascending twelve tone half series H=(H_1,..,H_6) in [0,..,11]^6 in 80 orbits H^G under the additive cyclic group G=Z/12Z of transpositions (interval shifts). By classification according to cardinality and forming the union of the orbits H^G and K^G of a half series H and its complement K, we obtain exactly the 44 Tropen by Josef Matthias Hauer, completely independent of symmetry properties, however, fundamentally due to so-called wider-gleiche orbits. This was not clear in previous literature.

column6: On Jacquet Modules of Principal Series in Families
column7: Let $G$ be a connected reductive group over a $p$-adic field $F$. Let $Y$ be the diagonalizable affine group scheme over $\mathbb{Z}[p^{-1},p^{1/2}]$ parametrizing weakly unramified characters of a minimal Levi $M$. The relative Weyl group $W$ acts on $Y$. We define a coherent sheaf $\mathcal{J}$, called the universal Jacquet module, on the fiber product $Y\times_{Y/\!/W}Y$. The fibers of $\mathcal{J}$ can be identified with the duals of spaces of intertwining operators between weakly unramified principal series representations of $G$. We use the geometry of $Y\times_{Y/\!/W}Y$ to study the fundamental properties of $\mathcal{J}$. In particular, we determine the invertible locus of $\mathcal{J}$. Thus we show that for any field $k$ with $\operatorname{char}k\neq p, p^{1/2}\in k$ and any weakly unramified character $χ\in Y(k)$, the normalized Jacquet module $π_{χ,N}$ of the normalized parabolic induction $π_χ=\operatorname{ind}_P^Gχ$ is isomorphic to $\mathcal{O}(χ\times_{Y/\!/W}Y)$ as an $\mathcal{O}(Y)$-module if and only if $\operatorname{End}_G(π_χ)\cong k$. This addresses the precise non-semisimple structure of Jacquet modules in the scalar endomorphism case. Specializing to the case in which $G$ is split, $χ$ is trivial, and $k=\mathbb{C}$, this proves a conjecture of Dipendra Prasad. We also show that the isomorphism $π_{χ,N}\cong\mathcal{O}(χ\times_{Y/\!/W}Y)$ cannot be defined canonically over the family of characters $χ$ satisfying $\operatorname{End}_G(π_χ)\cong\mathbb{C}$, by showing that the restriction of $\mathcal{J}$ to its invertible locus is a nontrivial line bundle if the relative root system of $G$ contains an irreducible component of rank at least two.

column5: Jean Lucien Randrianantenaina; Ali K. Uncu
column6: One more curious property of $1729$: The only Carmichael number of the form $2^np^3+1$ with prime $p$
column7: Florian Luca recently proved that if $2^np^3+1$ is a Carmichael number for some prime $p$ and integer $n\ge1$, then $p=3$. Here we complete the cubic classification by proving that $1729$, Hardy--Ramanujan taxicab number, is the only Carmichael number of the form $2^np^3+1$ with $p$ prime and $n\ge1$. The proof identifies the unique possible multiplicatively dependent prime factor, sharpens the known bound on Fermat prime factors of $2^nk+1$ from $k^2$ to $2k$, derives the explicit bound $n\le2742$, and concludes with a short sieve requiring neither factorisation nor primality testing.

column6: Finding four vertices of a square of area $n$ in a grid by geometric construction
column7: In this study, we consider geometric construction in an infinite square grid. Our purpose is to find efficient methods for constructing a square of area $n\in\mathbb{N}$ based on arithmetic properties of the sum of squares. As a consequence, for each $n\in\mathbb{N}$, we derive the optimal number of construction steps required to determine the four vertices of the square. Furthermore, we classify all positive integers into three classes according to these optimal numbers.

column6: On the self-extensions of the mod $p$ Jacquet-Langlands correspondence over $\mathbb{Q}_p$
column7: Let $p\ge5$ and $D$ be the unique nonsplit quaternion algebra over $\mathbb{Q}_p$. We compute, in the category of smooth representations with a fixed central character, the self-extension groups of the $D^{\times}$-representations occurring in the mod $p$ Jacquet-Langlands correspondence in the generic case. The main ingredient is a new weighted filtration on the relevant ring and module. The associated graded module preserves the first nontrivial extension relation, which is not detected by the $\mathfrak{m}_D$-adic filtration.

column6: An Explicit Uniform Connectivity Bound for Generalized Markoff Graphs
column7: Let $X_D$ be the surface $x^2+y^2+z^2-xyz=D$ over $\mathbb F_p$. For every prime $p>10^{320}$ and every $D\in\mathbb F_p\setminus\{4\}$, we prove that the three Vieta involutions act transitively on the trace triples of generating pairs of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb F_p)$. The proof combines an explicit primitive-fiber argument, Chen's orbit-size lower bound, and a weighted maximal-divisor estimate. We also give an explicit descent from Nielsen transitivity to transitivity under the Vieta involutions alone.

column6: Open Homomorphisms between $m$-step Solvable Galois Groups of Number Fields
column7: Let $K,L$ be number fields, and let $m \geq 2$ be an integer. In this paper, we prove that an open homomorphism $φ_{m+2}: G_K^{m+2} \to G_L^{m+2}$ induces an open homomorphism $φ_m$ that arises uniquely from a field embedding $τ_m:L_m \hookrightarrow K_m$. We first establish a sharper version of the $m$-step solvable cyclotomic compatibility criterion by Mao and Saïdi: if $φ_{m+2}:G_K^{m+2}\to G_L^{m+2}$ is compatible with the cyclotomic characters, then the induced map $φ_m:G_K^m \to G_L^m$ arises uniquely from a field embedding $L_m \hookrightarrow K_m$. Then we apply the strategy of OpenAI's (together with Tsujimura's recent explanation of OpenAI's work) proposed proof of Uchida's conjecture to show that every open homomorphism $φ_4:G_K^4 \to G_L^4$ is automatically compatible with the cyclotomic characters.

column6: Nine-Colored Partition Components Modulo 19
column7: Let $p_{m}(n)$ be the number of partitions of $n$ into parts of $m$ colors, and let $y=q^{19}$. Starting from Winquist's identity, as Hirschhorn did for the modulus $11$, we express each of the nineteen components of $(q;q)_{\infty}^{10}$ modulo $19$ as a sum of two quartic products of the theta functions $(y^{a};y^{19})_{\infty}(y^{19-a};y^{19})_{\infty}$, and deduce all nineteen generating functions $\sum_{n} p_{9}(19n+r)y^{n}$ modulo $19$ in closed form. The vanishing class $p_{9}(19n+17)$ is the one known previously. For seventeen colors, the residue class singled out by Kiming and Olsson carries no congruence, and we show that its generating function is $y f(y^{19})^{2}/f(y)$ modulo $19$. Along the way, we recall, with proofs, such exact relationships known for all these congruences. O'Brien's cubic relation is a Weierstrass equation for $X_{0}(19)$ in Kolberg's coordinates; we prove the existence of a doubling automorphism of the theta functions, fixing the cubic, which acts on both dissections by explicit scalars. All proofs are by hand.

column6: On metric multiplicative Diophantine approximation
column7: Gallagher's theorem (1962) gives a Khintchine-type dichotomy for the Lebesgue measure of the set of multiplicatively $ψ$-approximable points in $\mathbb{R}^n$, $n \geq 2$, for monotonic functions $ψ$. We establish this dichotomy for arbitrary functions $ψ$, proving a conjecture of Beresnevich, Haynes, and Velani (2013).

column6: Asymptotics for generalized integer partitions
column7: We study the asymptotic behavior of weighted partition functions $p_f(n)$, defined by the generating function $\prod_{n \geq 1} (1 - q^{n})^{-f(n)}$ with non-negative real weights $f(n)$. We assume that the associated Dirichlet series $D(s) = \sum_{n \geq 1} f(n) n^{-s}$ admits a meromorphic continuation to a half-plane $\Re(s) \geq -\varepsilon$, with finitely many real poles of arbitrary orders, the largest of which is a positive pole $α$ of order $k$, and a possibly infinite collection of complex poles lying strictly to the left of $α$, with some additional conditions. We extend the saddle-point method of Debruyne and Tenenbaum, and show that the pole $α$ dominates the contribution of all other poles. As a result, we give an explicit asymptotic formula for $p_f(n)$ described via generalized Lambert functions. Furthermore, we show that for $k \geq 2$ no finite combination of powers of $n$, $\log n$, $\log \log n, \ldots$ approximates the saddle point well enough to give an asymptotic formula for $p_f(n)$. We also discuss a number of applications related to algebra, number theory, and combinatorics.

column6: Dual Gauss-Thakur sums for Drinfeld modules
column7: We define dual Gauss-Thakur sums for Drinfeld modules, building on constructions of Gauss-Thakur sums due to Thakur, in the case of the Carlitz module, and Gazda and Maurischat, for general Anderson $t$-modules. Using results of Ferraro, we demonstrate that these sums can be obtained by evaluations of dual special functions at elements of finite fields. Our main results are matrix identities assembled from Gauss-Thakur sums and dual Gauss-Thakur sums in terms of multiplication coefficients for the Drinfeld module and its adjoint. We further prove determinant identities and explore connections with special Goss $L$-values and Drinfeld modular forms.

column6: On Hilbert's tenth problem for number fields
column7: Given a quadratic number field $K$ we show that the $abc$ conjecture over $K$ implies that $\mathbb{Z}$ is Diophantine in $K$ and, hence, a negative answer to Hilbert's tenth problem over $K$. More generally, the same conclusions hold for an arbitrary number field $K$ provided that the $abc$ conjecture holds over $K$ and that there is an elliptic curve over $\mathbb{Q}$ whose rank is positive and does not increase over $K$.

column5: Weidong Gao; Alfred Geroldinger; Guoqing Wang; Xiangneng Zeng
column6: A disproof of the van Emde Boas--Kruyswijk conjecture on the Davenport constant
column7: The Davenport constant $D(G)$ of a finite abelian group $G$ is the smallest positive integer $\ell$ such that every sequence $S$ with terms from $G$ and with length $|S| \ge \ell$ has a nontrivial zero-sum subsequence. A long-standing conjecture, first proposed by van Emde Boas and Kruyswijk in 1969, states that $D(C_n^r)=r(n-1)+1$ for all positive integers $n$ and $r$. We disprove this conjecture for every exponent $n=2k$ with $k\ge3$ odd. For each such $n$, we prove that $D(C_n^r)>r(n-1)+1$ for every $r\ge 8n-7$.

column6: Local-global compatibility with $p$-adic Langlands program for completed (co)homology of $\mathrm{GL}_2$ over CM fields
column7: For each place $v \mid p$ such that $F_v \simeq \mathbf{Q}_p$, we establish a compatibility with $p$-adic Langlands program for completed homology with integral coefficients for $\mathrm{GL}_2$ over CM fields $F$ with $[F:\mathbf{Q}]>2$, after localization with respect to a non-Eisenstein decomposed generic maximal ideal of a Hecke algebra.

column6: Sixth and twelfth moments of Dirichlet $L$-functions in prime power moduli
column7: For a fixed odd prime $p$ and $q=p^n$, we establish power-saving bounds for the sixth and twelfth moments of central values of primitive Dirichlet $L$-functions, with exponents $5/4-3/332$ and $2-51/261961$, respectively. More generally, our methods yield a power saving over the classical interpolation bound for every moment of order $4<j\le12$. Our approach begins with short second moments over character cosets and preserves the dependence on the character parameter. An exact linearization of the $p$-adic stationary phases reduces the critical large-value range to exponential sums with perturbed square-root phases over prime-power rings. We establish a large-value estimate for these sums by combining congruence-spacing bounds, higher congruence energies, and an average of quadratic Gauss sums over the dual frequency. For the remaining high-value range, we develop an incomplete-correlation estimate using $p$-adic exponent pairs.

column6: Two almost sure upper bounds for sums of random multiplicative functions
column7: Let $f,g$ be a squarefree and extended Rademacher random multiplicative functions, respectively. We prove that, for every $\varepsilon>0$, almost surely $$\big|\sum_{n \le x}\frac{f(n)}{\sqrt{n}}\big| \ll (\log\log x)^{1/4+\varepsilon}, \qquad \big|\sum_{n\le x}g(n)\big|\ll\sqrt{x}(\log\log x)^{1/4+\varepsilon}.$$ We also show that almost surely, there exist arbitrarily large values of $x$ such that $\sum_{n \le x}\frac{f(n)}{\sqrt{n}} \gg (\log\log x)^{1/4+o(1)}$. We follow Caich and Durkan and Pearce-Crump by using a version of the Azuma--Hoeffding inequality for martingale difference sequences.

column6: Divisibility of Character Values of Wreath Products of Symmetric Groups
column7: Let $G$ be a finite group whose character table is integer-valued, and let $K$ be any fixed positive integer. We prove that almost every entry of the character table of the wreath product $G\wr S_N$ is divisible by $K$ as $N\to\infty$.

column6: The Ceresa Cycle on $X_0^+(p)$
column7: We consider the curve $X_0^+(p)$ with prime $p$, which is the quotient of the modular curve $X_0(p)$ by the Fricke involution. We describe how one can explicitly calculate the shadow of a Hecke operator on $X_0^+(p)$, which is a rational divisor on $X_0^+(p)$ whose nonvanishing is an obstruction to the Ceresa cycle of $X_0^+(p)$ being torsion in the Chow group of the Jacobian of $X_0^+(p)$. We also provide an implementation of this procedure in PARI/GP and SageMath and use this on all primes below 5000.

column6: Cameron--Martin theorem for SLE welding measures
column7: For $κ\in(0,4]$, we prove a Cameron--Martin theorem for the welding law induced by SLE$_κ$ loop measure. Under simultaneous left and right composition $h\mapsto\varphi\circ h\circψ^{-1}$, the transformed law is mutually absolutely continuous with respect to the original law exactly when both maps belong to the Weil--Petersson group, and is mutually singular otherwise. Thus the Weil--Petersson group is the quasi-invariance group of the welding law under composition on either side. We also prove that it is its own normalizer in the group of orientation-preserving circle homeomorphisms. For Weil--Petersson pairs, we derive an explicit Radon--Nikodym derivative in terms of a relative action well defined for SLE weldings and prove that it belongs to $L^{1+\varepsilon}$ for some $\varepsilon>0$ depending on the pair.

column6: On the refined Kaneko--Zagier conjecture
column7: We extend our results on Zhao's conjectural basis to finite multiple zeta values modulo arbitrary prime powers and to the corresponding completed algebra. As a consequence, the refined Kaneko--Zagier conjecture, which gives a precise description of relations modulo arbitrary prime powers in terms of ordinary multiple zeta values, follows from the dimension and direct-sum conjectures for ordinary and finite multiple zeta values. We also prove Rosen's lifting conjecture under the dimension conjecture for finite multiple zeta values. The proofs use confluence relations and $p$-adic associators and do not use motivic theory.

column6: Low Moments, Small Balls and Star Discrepancy
column7: Let $D_P$ be the discrepancy function of a configuration $P$ of $N$ points in the $d$-dimensional unit cube, and let $\|D_P\|_q$ be its $L^q$ discrepancy. We prove that for all fixed $d\ge2$ and $0<q\le1$ the $L^q$ discrepancy of every configuration of $N\ge2$ points is at least $c_{d,q}(\log N)^{(d-1)/2}$ with a constant $c_{d,q}>0$. This bound is sharp; together with the classical results for $q>1$, it determines the minimal order of the $L^q$ discrepancy for every $0<q<\infty$ in every dimension $d\ge2$, and for $q=1$ it answers Chen's problem on the sharp lower bound for the $L^1$ discrepancy in dimension $d\ge3$. We prove the small ball inequality for Haar functions in every fixed dimension $d\ge3$ and for arbitrary real coefficients with the conjectured power of $n$, up to a polylogarithmic factor; here $2^{-n}$ is the smallest volume of the dyadic boxes involved. The method also extends to a class of piecewise polynomial mother functions. For the $L^\infty$ discrepancy $\|D_P\|_\infty=ND^*(P)$, where $D^*(P)$ is the star discrepancy, we prove the conjectured lower bound $c(\log N)^{3/2}$ in dimension three, and the lower bound $(\log N)^{d/2}$ up to a power of $\log\log N$ in every fixed dimension $d\ge4$. Finally, we construct $N$-point sets whose $L^\infty$ discrepancy is $O_d((\log N)^{d-1-1/16})$ in every fixed dimension $d\ge3$; this disproves the conjectured optimality of the order $(\log N)^{d-1}$ of the classical constructions.

column6: Orbits of $p$-adic flows: balls, time-one maps and minimal group actions
column7: Let $f$ be a vector field on $\mathbb{Z}_p^d$ given by polynomials, or by power series converging on $\mathbb{Z}_p^d$, whose coefficients are divisible by $p^c$, where $c \ge 1$ ($c \ge 2$ when $p = 2$). Its flow exists for every $p$-adic time. I show that $t \mapsto \varphi_t(x)$ multiplies distances by exactly $\|f(x)\|_p$, in every dimension. This gives explicit flow-box coordinates, closed formulas for hitting times, return times and orbit averages, and a Newton iteration that computes them with quadratic convergence; in dimension one it recovers Mukhamedov's theorem that interpolated orbits are balls. I then show that the analytic maps $g$ congruent to the identity modulo $p^c$, coefficientwise, are exactly the time-one maps of such fields, and that the field is congruent to $g - \mathrm{id}$ modulo $p^{c+1}$. So the interpolated iterates of Bell and Poonen are flows of this kind, and I obtain a quantitative minimality criterion: if the displacements $g_i(x_0) - x_0$ of $d$ such maps span $p^k\mathbb{Z}_p^d$, the group they generate acts minimally on the ball of radius $p^{-k}$ about $x_0$. Where the argument of Cantat and Jang gives an orbit closure containing some open set, this names the ball, at every level $k$ and in every dimension; for $d = 2$ and $k = 1$ it is Jang's criterion for Markoff surfaces, which I test numerically at $7830$ points. Finally, the formal logarithm of $\mathbb{G}_m$ or of an elliptic curve is the rectifying coordinate of an explicit field, so the local divisibility $v_p([t]z) = v_p(z) + v_p(t)$ for $v_p(z) \ge 1 + c$, deep in the kernel of reduction, follows from the metric identity alone.

column6: On Hilbert's tenth problem over a quadratic field
column7: In 2026, OpenAI proved that Hilbert's Tenth Problem over the field $\mathbb Q$ of rational numbers has a negative solution. In this paper we study Hilbert's Tenth Problem over the quadratic field $K=\mathbb Q(\sqrt2)$. We prove that there is no algorithm to decide for any polynomial equation $P(x_1,\ldots,x_{48})=0$ with integer coefficients whether it has solutions with $x_1,\ldots,x_{48}\in K$. We also show the existence of a polynomial $f(x_0,x_1,\ldots,x_{25})$ with integer coefficients such that $a\in K$ is a rational integer if and only if $f(a,x_1,\ldots,x_{25})=0$ for some $x_1,\ldots,x_{25}\in K$.

column6: On the Erdős--Ginzburg--Ziv problem for $\mathbb Z_n^3$
column7: The Erdős--Ginzburg--Ziv constant $\mathsf s(\mathbb Z_n^r)$ is the least positive integer $t$ such that every sequence of $t$ elements of $\mathbb Z_n^r$ contains $n$ terms whose sum is zero. In this paper, we prove that $$\mathsf s(\mathbb Z_n^3)=9n+o(n)$$ for odd $n$. For every fixed $r\ge 4$, we also show that $\mathsf s(\mathbb Z_n^r)\le\bigl(\binom{2r-1}{r}+1\bigr)n+o_r(n).$ Our approach combines Alon--Dubiner-type spectral expansion, Zakharov's convex-geometric framework, and restricted-sum ideas developed by Han and Ren.

column6: Self-adjoint skew quartics, symplectic monodromy, and zeta functions
column7: For an odd prime power $P$, let $A_H(P)$ be the number of $a\in\F_{P^H}$ for which the self-adjoint skew quartic $t^4+t^3+at^2+t+1$ is irreducible in $\F_{P^H}[t;σ]$, with $σ(c)=c^P$. We determine $A_H(3)$ for every $H\ge1$ and prove that its minimal constant-coefficient recurrence has order $24$. Local ramification gives the degrees of the Steinberg and regular cuspidal Frobenius polynomials. Duality and finitely many exact counts determine both polynomials. For $P=p^f$ with $p\nmid f$, we construct an explicit genus-$P(P+1)/2$ flag curve whose zeta numerator is the Steinberg Frobenius polynomial. At $P=3$ this identifies the degree-$12$ factor computed above with the zeta numerator of a genus-$6$ curve. For general $P$ the flag curve and the regular cuspidal factors give a rational expression for the counting series. We evaluate the linear coefficients of the two factors by an elliptic-curve point count and express their quadratic coefficients through a single finite-field character sum.

column6: On the ring of bounded functions on the character variety
column7: Let $\mathfrak{X}$ denote the character variety associated to the group $(o_L, +)$, where $o_L$ is the ring of integers in a finite extension $L/\mathbb{Q}_p$. $\mathfrak{X}$ is a rigid analytic variety parametrizing locally $L$-analytic characters. Let $Λ_L\left(\mathfrak{X}\right)$ denote the global sections bounded by $1$. In this paper we prove that $Λ_L\left(\mathfrak{X}\right)= o_L[[o_L]]$, answering the question posed in [AB24].

column6: The rational points of the non-split Cartan modular curve of level 121
column7: We prove that the modular curve $X_{\mathrm{ns}}^{+}(121)$ of the normalizer of a non-split Cartan subgroup of level 121, of genus 511, has exactly seven rational points, all of them CM. This is the level 121 case of a conjecture of Rouse, Sutherland and Zureick-Brown, and with their theorem it determines the 11-adic images of Galois of non-CM elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q}$. The Jacobian has rank equal to the genus. At $p = 17$ and $43$ one Hecke block of the Mordell-Weil group has logarithm divisible by $p^2$ but $p$-adic height of valuation one, and a comparison of valuations in the quadratic Chabauty identity then shows that each CM point is the only rational point in its residue disc, with no computation of the local height at $p$, no basis of the Mordell-Weil group and no equations for the curve. The inputs come from expansions of differentials at CM points and from a formula we prove for intersection numbers of CM divisors of coprime fundamental discriminants under Hecke operators on $X_{\mathrm{ns}}^{+}(\ell^e)$ (Theorem 1.3).

column6: A Hopf algebra action on the cohomology of moduli of abelian varieties
column7: We show that the rational compactly supported cohomology of the moduli space $\mathcal{A} = \bigsqcup_{g \geq 0} \mathcal{A}_g$ of principally polarized abelian varieties is free as a bigraded module over the Hopf algebra formed by its weight-zero subspace. The action arises from a symplectic analog of the Waldhausen $S$-construction. This structure yields new lower bounds for Betti numbers and the dimensions of the graded pieces of the weight filtration on the cohomology of $\mathcal{A}_g$. In particular, $\dim H_c^{2g + k}(\mathcal{A}_g)$ grows at least exponentially with $g$ for every nonnegative $k \neq 1, 3$. We also give conjectural descriptions of the full mixed Hodge structures in genera four and five, and of mixed Tate subquotients of $H_c^{2g}(\mathcal{A}_g)$ associated with shuffle algebras and multiple zeta values in every genus.

column5: Jeremy Miller; Urshita Pal; Peter Patzt
column6: Comodule algebras and the cohomology of symplectic groups
column7: We prove that the homology of symplectic groups with Steinberg module coefficients forms a comodule algebra over the homology of general linear groups with Steinberg module coefficients. We prove a freeness-type result for comodule algebras. We deduce new lower bounds for the high-dimensional cohomology of symplectic groups of number rings and their congruence subgroups.

column6: Arithmetic Upper and Lower Bounds for the Denumerant Function II
column7: We apply the elementary arithmetic argument of the first paper of this series (arXiv:2204.13689) to binomial coefficients, and obtain upper and lower bounds for Sylvester's denumerant function for arbitrary positive integers $a_1,\dots,a_k$ that sharpen those of Agnarsson. The lower bound is a sum of binomial coefficients; it holds along the multiples of $\gcd(a_1,\dots,a_k)$ without assuming that a solution exists, and it is greater than the polynomial lower bound of the first paper. In the upper bound the shift of Agnarsson's binomial coefficient is reduced.

column6: Algebraic independence of $v$-adic Carlitz multiple polylogarithms via period interpretations
column7: Based on Hartl's de Rham-crystalline comparison isomorphism, we formulate a notion of André's $v$-adic periods for a class of Anderson $\mathbb{F}_q[z]$-motives with respect to a degree-one finite place $v$ of a rational function field over a finite field, following Ancona-Frăţilă's formulation of $p$-adic periods. The formulation naturally produces deformation series of the resulting periods and Frobenius difference equations satisfied by these series. We then explain how the formulation brings the resulting $v$-adic periods within the scope of Chen's $v$-adic ABP criterion and of difference Galois theory, and gives us a strategy to study the transcendence degrees of $v$-adic periods through their deformation series. We show that certain special values of $v$-adic Carlitz multiple polylogarithms can be expressed in terms of André's $v$-adic periods. Applying the strategy to these examples, we obtain algebraic independence results for certain special values of $v$-adic Carlitz multiple polylogarithms; more precisely, the transcendence degree of the field generated by a suitable collection of special values of $v$-adic Carlitz multiple polylogarithms is one less than the transcendence degree of the field generated by the corresponding special values of $\infty$-adic Carlitz multiple polylogarithms together with the Carlitz period.

column5: Alan Filipin; Yasutsugu Fujita; Ana Jurasić
column6: On the non-extendibility of triangular $D(n)$-pairs $\{n,2n\}$ with $n = 2k^2 \pm k$
column7: We study a class of Diophantine problems arising from triangular analogues of classical Diophantine tuples. A set of positive integers is called a triangular $D(n)$-tuple if the product of any two distinct elements, increased by $n$, is a triangular number. In this paper, we investigate the extensibility of triangular $D(n)$-pairs of the form $\{n,2n\}$, where $n = 2k^2 + \varepsilon k$, with $k$ an odd positive integer and $\varepsilon \in \{-1,1\}$ such that $4k + \varepsilon$ is prime. We prove that for all $(k,\varepsilon)$ in a finite explicitly determined set, the pair $\{n,2n\}$ cannot be extended to a triangular $D(n)$-quadruple. The obtained results give further evidence for a general non-extensibility phenomenon, which we formulate as a conjecture.

column5: Armando Gutierrez Terradillos; Lois Omil-Pazos; Óscar Rivero
column6: Exceptional zeros for $\mathrm{GSp}(4) \times \mathrm{GL}(2)$ and Yoshida lifts
column7: The aim of this article is to study an exceptional zero phenomenon for the $p$-adic $L$-functions attached to $\mathrm{GSp}_4\times\mathrm{GL}_2$ in the critical regions (F) and (D). We construct improved $p$-adic $L$-functions by replacing the $p$-depleted Eisenstein family with its $p$-ordinary counterpart. Under a local compatibility hypothesis at the ramified places and classical control for the families, we show that their poles detect exactly the Yoshida lifts whose smaller constituent is dual to the $\mathrm{GL}_2$ representation. The proof compares their residues with distinguished automorphic periods, extending the coherent period formula to the case where one modular form has weight zero. An explicit Euler-factor identity relates each improved function to the usual $p$-adic $L$-function. At these Yoshida points, the vanishing factor cancels the pole, and the resulting value is expressed through the distinguished period and the logarithmic derivative of the ordinary elliptic root. We also discuss the expected factorization along Yoshida families into Hida--Rankin $p$-adic $L$-functions.

column6: Large Gaps Between Piatetski-Shapiro Primes
column7: A Piatetski-Shapiro prime is a prime number that can be written as $\lfloor m^c \rfloor$ for some positive integer $m$ and non-integer $c>1$. Li and Pan showed the results for small gaps between consecutive Piatetski-Shapiro primes for $1<c<9/8$. On the other hand, Deshouillers, Drmota, and Müllner showed the large gaps between Piatetski-Shapiro primes although they did not mention it explicitly whenever there are infinitely many Piatetski-Shapiro primes with exponent $c$ using binomial expansion. In this article, we use a different method from theirs, and we obtain the explicit exponent that appears in their paper.

column6: Proof Checking Continuous Reachability
column7: This paper introduces a proof format and proof checker for certifying reachability computations of ordinary differential equations (ODEs) with polynomial vector fields. Establishing a proof checking framework for certifying ODE reachability is similar to the checking of UNSAT proofs for propositional satisfiability solving, but it is even more important due to the challenges inherent in dealing with ODEs, and even more challenging due to the numerical nature of ODE reachability algorithms. The proofs are expressed in differential dynamic logic (dL), and can be independently verified with symbolic theorem provers for dL (e.g. KeYmaeraX). Such proofs are naturally generated by reachability algorithms based on Taylor models, a popular technique to obtain rigorous bounds on approximations of ODEs. This paper proves the completeness of such proofs - if an approximation was correctly computed by some (possibly untrusted) reachability algorithm via Taylor models, then a corresponding proof in dL can be automatically generated and checked to be correct in dL's proof calculus. A dedicated proof checker is implemented in Lean4 for improved performance, which is capable of formally verifying benchmarks in the ARCH competition.

column6: Arithmetic Upper and Lower Bounds for the Denumerant Function III
column7: We extend the denumerant to a weighted denumerant, the sum of a function $μ$ over the solutions in non-negative integers of $a_1x_1+\cdots+a_kx_k=n$. For the monomial weights $x_1^{α_1}\cdots x_k^{α_k}$, with exponents $α_i\in\mathbb{R}_{\geq0}$, we prove upper and lower bounds of the kind of those of the first paper of this series (arXiv:2204.13689), with an explicit constant and explicit shifts. As an example of application, summing these bounds over all the numbers $a_1,\dots,a_k$ we find, by elementary means, the asymptotic main term of the sums $\sum_{y_1+\cdots+y_k=n}σ_{α_1}(y_1)\cdotsσ_{α_k}(y_k)$ of products of divisor functions, for every $k$ and for real exponents $α_i\neq0$ of either sign.

column5: Andrés R. Moreno; José L. Ramírez
column6: The Semi--Fibonacci Partition Tree
column7: In this work, we introduce a binary tree in which every semi-Fibonacci partition appears exactly once. The left--right address of a vertex gives an explicit formula for the parts of the corresponding partition and encodes statistics such as the largest $2$-adic valuation among its parts. We construct a sign-reversing involution that refines Andrews's parity theorem by determining the difference between the numbers of partitions of a given integer at even and odd depths. Inspired by properties of the Calkin--Wilf tree, we study several parameters of our tree and use them to obtain new results on semi-Fibonacci partitions. We also derive generating functions for partition statistics and determine the average and extremal partition sizes at each level.

column6: Certified pandigital approximations of $π$, $γ$, $δ$ and $e$
column7: In 2004 Erich Friedman asked for the best approximations of $π$, $e$, the Euler-Mascheroni constant $γ$ and Feigenbaum's constant $δ$ that use each of the digits $1,\dots,n$ exactly once, with addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, exponentiation, parentheses and the decimal point. We determine the optimal expressions for $π$, $γ$ and $δ$ for every $n \le 9$, with the digits in any order and in increasing order, and for $e$ when $n \le 6$. The optima are found by exhaustive search and certified by an independent algorithm that encloses every expression rigorously and decides each candidate with Arb and exact arithmetic; a second certified computation covers intermediate values of any size. Twenty-one entries improve the published records; for $π$ with the digits 1-9 the optimal error is $2.81\cdot 10^{-14}$. For $e$, whose records come from identities between power towers, we prove that Bamberger's formula is optimal within the natural family of such identities. All code and certificates are public.

column6: Rational Elliptic Period Relations Across Realizations: Complex Lattices, Local p-adic Periods, and Drinfeld Modules
column7: We determine the algebraic relations among full de Rham comparison periods of elliptic curves over finite extensions of $\mathbb Q_p$. The connected local monodromy group gives the transcendence degree and an explicit affine linear relation ideal for the full matrix in Fontaine's field $B_{\mathrm{dR}}$. After normalizing the holomorphic row and reducing to $\mathbb C_p$, the transcendence degree drops by one and the normalized determinant supplies the additional relation. Every polynomial relation of degree at most $d$ is detected modulo $t^{d+1}$. For $d\ge1$ this bound is sharp for each elliptic curve. A rational quasi-period row gives a Galois-stable Tate line. Together with an algebraic holomorphic period ratio it forces potential splitting, which identifies the exact ordinary CM obstruction. We compute the full Tate matrix. For ordinary non-CM curves with $p\ge5$, the standard quasi-period row is rational precisely at a zero of Katz's $E_{2,p}$. Away from the zeros the two full ratios are algebraically independent. At the zeros, a nonzero quasi-period and the normalized holomorphic ratio have algebraically independent images in $\mathbb C_p$. The complex question that motivates these results, the analogue for Drinfeld modules, and a conditional arithmetic consequence for Katz values complete the comparison.

column6: Note on the largest prime factors of consecutive integers II
column7: For an integer $n > 1$, let $P^+(n)$ be the largest prime factor of $n$. We show that a positive proportion of integers $n\leq x$ satisfy\begin{align*} P^+(n-1)<P^+(n)>P^+(n+1)<P^+(n+2)>P^+(n+3). \end{align*} The proof employs Selberg's upper-bound sieve and the multidimensional Selberg sieve developed in the Polymath8b work.

column5: Ryutaro Misawa; Masanori Sawa; Filip Špiranec
column6: Rational Designs and Prouhet--Tarry--Escott Problems
column7: For every strength, we prove the existence of rational designs on spheres, orthogonal and unitary groups, real and complex Grassmannians, and ellipsoids that are defined by positive-definite quadratic forms with rational coefficients and have a rational point. This answers Bannai's Problem for these spaces, solves the problem of Cui--Xia--Xiang on rational spherical $4$-designs on the unit circle, and proves Xiang's conjecture in the stronger form of existence in every dimension. To this end, we introduce the $(G,\mathcal{S})$-Prouhet--Tarry--Escott problem for an abelian group $G$ and a finite set of characters $\mathcal{S}$ and develop its existence and minimality theory. We also prove a general theorem transforming integer-weighted rational designs into equi-weighted designs on distinct rational points. On the unit circle $\mathbb{S}^1$, we determine the minimum sizes of rational spherical designs of strengths $4,5,6,7$ and show that they are respectively $2304,4608,9216,9216$. We also show that the minimum size of a rational spherical $5$-design on $\mathbb{S}^2$ is $192$. We further apply our framework to prove a conjecture of Thuswaldner--Ziegler on sums of distinct units and to answer Mahabaduge's problem on convex equilateral lattice polygons affirmatively.

column6: A sharp bounded bijection for tight cylindric partitions
column7: Fix a cyclic profile of coprime rank $r$ and level $\ell$, both at least three, and an entry bound $n\ge1$. Let $d$ be the deficit from the maximum volume of a tight cylindric partition. For $d\le n\min(r,\ell)$, the one-row combinatorial $R$ matches the tight cylinders whose last slice lies inside the maximizer's last slice with the partitions of $d$ in which each part occurs fewer than $r$ times. The inverse preserves the profile and entry bound. We identify every partition missed at the next deficit. A prefix test decides whether any cylinder lies outside this sector and, if so, identifies the unique one of least deficit. This explains the leading coefficient gap in Warnaar's $Q_{n,c}$. We also determine the first correction to the vertex terms of the published bounded determinant.

column5: Yi Zhou; Jiaheng Zhuang; Shuguo Zhang
column6: Rigidity of ordinal spaces
column7: A Hausdorff space $Y$ is called rigid if, for every positive integer $k$, every continuous open $k$-to-one map $p:X\to Y$ from a Hausdorff space $X$ admits a partition of $X$ into $k$ open sets, each mapped homeomorphically onto $Y$. We show that the Sorgenfrey plane is not rigid, giving negative answers in $\mathsf{ZFC}$ to Velichko's questions on finite products of rigid spaces and on strongly zero-dimensional spaces. For ordinal spaces, we prove in $\mathsf{ZF}$ that every regular uncountable cardinal with the tree property is rigid. In $\mathsf{ZFC}$, we obtain a characterization for arbitrary limit ordinals: a limit ordinal $α$ is rigid if and only if every coherent family $\langle f_ξ:ξ<α\rangle$, where $f_ξ:ξ\to\{0,1\}$, admits a uniformization. As a consequence, a limit ordinal is rigid if and only if its cofinality is rigid. The characterization also implies that $ω_1$ is not rigid in $\mathsf{ZFC}$, answering a question of Velichko.

column5: Bart De Bruyn; Sergey Goryainov; Yilin Xie; Weihao Yan; Ferdinando Zullo
column6: Fourier bases for square-order Paley graphs
column7: Let $q$ be an odd prime power and consider the Paley graph $P(q^2)$ on the finite field $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$. A well-known optimal eigenfunction of this graph is supported on the norm-one subgroup, where it takes the values $1$ and $-1$ on the two cosets of its subgroup of index two. Its support has the minimum possible size $q+1$. Starting from this eigenfunction, we construct a family of multiplicative translates and prove that they form a basis of the space of complex-valued functions on $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}^{\times}$. After extending these functions to the whole field, the translates indexed by squares form a basis of one nonprincipal eigenspace of the Paley graph, while those indexed by nonsquares form a basis of the other. In particular, both nonprincipal eigenspaces admit bases consisting entirely of optimal eigenfunctions. The main ingredient is a multiplicative Fourier analysis of the shifted eigenfunction. We determine the moduli of all its Fourier coefficients and, in particular, show that none of them vanishes.

column6: The Riemann Hypothesis and Prime Numbers
column7: The Riemann hypothesis is attracting a great deal of attention at present. It is one of the seven Millennium Prize Problems in mathematics, for each of which the Clay Mathematics Institute offers a prize of one million dollars. It is arguably the most important open problem in all of mathematics. Numerous results have so far been proved only under the assumption of the Riemann hypothesis. Yet the hypothesis itself sounds rather dull: it conjectures that the zeros of a certain function have a certain form. Things become truly exciting, however, when we look at its connection with prime numbers, and that is what we shall do here.

column6: Block decimation and perfect actions for $p$-adic valued path integrals
column7: In earlier work we introduced a finite-partition propagator for $\mathbb{C}_p$-valued wave functions, in which the intermediate positions are integrated against atomic measures. The iterated integral evaluates the action on the equally spaced chain between the endpoints, so each partition level is obtained by iterating an exact, tree-level block decimation of two-point lattice actions, with no integration over fluctuations. This kinematic decimation is the Fréchet derivative, at the free actions, of the variational decimation underlying classical perfect actions. Since the time step $p^n$ is small in the real norm exactly when it is large $p$-adically, refinement and coarsening (the ultraviolet and infrared directions over $\mathbb{R}$) exchange roles, and each yields one limit. Under refinement, potentials supported on $\mathbb{Z}_p$, given there by a convergent power series, and entering the slice action without the time-step weight produce an interaction that stabilizes off the diagonal after finitely many steps and converges uniformly on $\mathbb{Z}_p^2$, with sharp error $p^{-M}$ after $M$ steps, to a scale-covariant (perfect) action, governed near the diagonal by a Volkenborn integral; with the weight no limit exists. For the harmonic oscillator no refinement limit exists at fixed frequency, but under coarsening the variational flow is solved in closed form: the lattice angle is multiplied by $p$ at each step, the coupling obeys a Chebyshev recursion, no caustic occurs, and the rescaled action converges to a free action with renormalized mass $m_0\sin_p(θ_0)/θ_0$. The rescaled linearized map is diagonalizable on polynomial actions with eigenvalues $p^{2-b}$, so directions relevant over $\mathbb{R}$ are irrelevant over $\mathbb{Q}_p$ and conversely.

column6: The distribution of greatest common divisors of binomial coefficients and their upper indices
column7: For positive integers $n,d$, let $A_d(n)$ denote the number of integers $0\le k\le n$ such that $\gcd\bigl(n,\binom nk\bigr)=d$, and put $S_d(x)=\sum_{n\le x}A_d(n)$. We prove that, for each fixed integer $d\ge2$, \[ S_d(x)\sim\frac{d-1}{d}\,\mathfrak c\,\frac{x}{\log x}\qquad(x\to\infty),\qquad \mathfrak c=1.526453\ldots \] The key step is to extend the coprimality result of Ford and Konyagin to arbitrary fixed parameters $d\ge2$ and $1\le j<d$, obtaining \[ \#\Bigl\{m\le x:\gcd\Bigl(m,\binom{dm}{jm}\Bigr)=1\Bigr\} \sim\mathfrak c\frac x{\log x}. \] The zero set of the corresponding Kummer carry function is a finite union of intervals of total measure $1/2$. We combine this property with estimates for small prime factors, Selberg trigonometric approximation, and exponential sum estimates over primes to count simultaneous carry conditions. We further prove that, for every fixed integer $e\ge1$, \[ \#\Bigl\{m\le x:\gcd\Bigl(m,\binom{dm}{jm}\Bigr)=e\Bigr\} \sim\frac{\mathfrak c}{e}\frac x{\log x}. \]

column6: Computational trust as intuitionistic knowledge
column7: In this paper, we will argue that the notion of computational trust can be understood as a form of fallible intuitionistic knowledge grounded in verification. This approach naturally captures a key aspect of trust: it involves vulnerability. Specifically, it validates the principle that verification leads to trust but does not validate the opposite principle that trust leads to verification. Thus, we can trust on good grounds that some program will perform according to its specification but the program might still fail. We present a simple logic for capturing this notion of computational trust based on constructive modal propositional logic extended with a trust modality, which will be specified in an inferential fashion and by utilizing the proofs-as-programs correspondence.

column6: $p$-adic Fourier theory for unramified extensions of $\mathbb{Q}_p$ and weighted Monna maps
column7: We generalize a recent result of Ardakov and Berger on the $p$-adic valuations of Schneider--Teitelbaum polynomials evaluated at Lubin--Tate periods over the unramified quadratic extension of $\mathbb{Q}_p$. For finite unramified extensions of $\mathbb{Q}_p$ of degree $f \geq 2$, we introduce a weighted analogue of the Monna map and show that it determines the valuations of these polynomial values for Lubin--Tate formal groups whose formal logarithms are $p$-typical. Our proof uses the Artin--Hasse exponential and Witt vectors. As an application, for a distinguished Lubin--Tate formal group, we determine the exact norms of the associated Schneider--Teitelbaum polynomials on Banach spaces of locally analytic functions and obtain an explicit rescaling of the Banach basis constructed by Bannai and Kobayashi so that each basis element has norm one.

column6: Moduli spaces of $(3,6)$-$K3$ surfaces and cubic surfaces
column7: We compare the ball quotient for marked nodal cubic surfaces with the arithmetic quotient of a domain of type IV associated with $K3$ surfaces arising from configurations of six lines in $\mathbb{P}^2$. Using the Coble map and the period mapping associated with the hypergeometric system of type $(3,6)$, we identify a common open subset of the GIT quotient of six ordered points in $\mathbb{P}^2$ and the ball quotient. This identification gives an analog in dimension four of the Janus-like phenomenon for the Segre cubic and the Igusa quartic, making precise a comparison suggested by Allcock, Carlson, and Toledo. For a related family of lattice-polarized $K3$ surfaces, we give a geometric realization of the ring of meromorphic modular forms with prescribed poles and trivial character and describe the corresponding Looijenga compactification.

column6: Exponential generating functions of multiple polylogarithms at arbitrary integer indices
column7: We give an explicit formula expressing any finite product of depth-one polylogarithms at arbitrary integer indices as a $\mathbb{Q}$-linear combination of shuffle-type multivariable multiple polylogarithms. The proof starts with an exponential generating function. For any fixed positive multi-index $\mathbf{s}=(s_1,\ldots,s_r)$, the substitution $z_i\mapsto z_i\exp(x_1+\cdots+x_i)$ in the corresponding shuffle-type multiple polylogarithm yields the exponential generating function for the functions at indices $\mathbf{s}-\mathbf{k}$, where $\mathbf{k}$ ranges over $\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}^r$. We combine this identity with the shuffle product for iterated integrals at positive indices and compare coefficients to obtain the product formula. The appendix gives an alternative proof using the Euler differential operators $z_i\partial/\partial z_i$.

column6: Mahler measures and a cubic Dedekind zeta value in three dilogarithms
column7: A general formula evaluates a three-variable Mahler measure at Heegner points of fundamental discriminant $-d$, with $d>3$ and $d\equiv3\pmod8$, using CM modular forms and ray class $L$-values. Together with the case $d=27$, it proves six identities conjectured by Zheng. The parameter at $d=163$ also occurs in a cubic Ramanujan-Sato series for $1/π$. For $C=\mathbb Q(a)$, where $a^3+2a-2=0$, an exact hyperbolic volume argument expresses the Dedekind zeta derivative $ζ_C'(-1)$ in three Bloch-Wigner dilogarithms. The analogous identity for $C(\sqrt5)$ remains conjectural and is reduced to one explicit Bloch-group equality.

column6: Prime-Power Expansions and Boundary Corrections for the Secular Coefficients of Riemann-Zero Windows
column7: We study the secular coefficients of characteristic polynomials attached to finite windows of zeros of the Riemann zeta function, mapped onto the unit circle. Starting from the Riemann-von Mangoldt formula and Newton's identities, we derive a symmetric prime-power model for their generating function. The model carries an explicit boundary factor $(1-w)^{-ΔS}$, where $ΔS$ is the variation of $S(t)$ across the window. The boundary correction is determined by the integer zero count of the window rather than by a fitted parameter. For finite prime-power tails we prove a mean-square identity with an explicit diagonal term and an explicit error bound, using the Montgomery-Vaughan generalisation of Hilbert's inequality. Numerical experiments near $T = 10^6$, on computed but uncertified zeros, show that prime powers up to $Q = 32$, the zero count of the window and the known smooth term reproduce the secular coefficients. The median relative residual energy is $1.3 \times 10^{-4}$ for $H = 181$ and $1.0 \times 10^{-5}$ for $H = 724$; the means are $2.1 \times 10^{-3}$ and $2.7 \times 10^{-3}$. The error is strongly asymmetric across windows. An exact convolution identity separates a residual, whose measured size does not depend on the boundary exponent, from its amplification by the boundary factor; the measured amplification follows the exponent over eight orders of magnitude. The diagonal prediction matches the measured power-sum residuals within 16% in the tested regimes. Exact identities and finite Dirichlet-polynomial estimates are kept separate from the numerical reconstruction. Extending the mean-square estimate to the true $S(t)$ is open and appears tied to pair correlations of zeros. This note does not propose a route to the Riemann hypothesis.

column6: Exact Differential Spectra for Five Families of Power Functions
column7: For a power function over a finite field, differential uniformity records only the largest entry of its differential distribution table, whereas the differential spectrum records every multiplicity and its frequency. We determine exact differential spectra for five families of low-uniformity power functions in odd characteristic, including families previously studied primarily through uniformity bounds. Our methods combine spectrum-preserving exponent changes, factorial moments, intersections of injective images, character sums, and point counts on curves over finite fields. For the ternary family of Yuan, Du, Qiao, and Zhou, we give a fixed-cover formula and an explicit Artin factorization for one pair-intersection cover; its odd-degree counts reduce to traces of elliptic and genus-two curves. Inverse-cubic powers yield a conic evaluation in characteristic five and low-genus trace formulas in larger characteristics. Four ternary branches associated with Dobbertin, Mills, Müller, Pott, and Willems share one complete spectrum governed by an elliptic trace. For the Yan--Han family, an Artin--Prym decomposition gives all multiplicity frequencies and exact differential uniformity, including a planar endpoint. For Felke's family, we express extension-field spectra as one-dimensional character sums while identifying the known prime-field cases. A standalone program independently reproduces the finite-field calculations used in the proofs.

column6: Uninorm constructions on bounded trellises via closure and interior operators
column7: In this paper, we establish necessary and sufficient conditions under which six closure- or interior-based operations on bounded trellises are uninorms. These operations incorporate triangular norms, triangular conorms, or both, and form three order-dual pairs. Since the underlying pseudo-order need not be transitive and meet and join need not be associative, standard lattice arguments do not apply directly. Under a fixed ambient transitivity assumption, the first pair is characterized by image, monotonicity, and compatibility conditions for the associated maps on elements incomparable with the neutral element; an additional comparison condition used in earlier sufficient constructions is shown to be redundant. Complete characterizations are also obtained for the variants with an absorbing endpoint, including both nondegenerate and degenerate interval cases. For the pair involving both a triangular norm and a triangular conorm, we derive exact comparison conditions requiring the triangular norm to take the value~$0$, or dually the triangular conorm to take the value~$1$, in the relevant cases. These conditions reduce to the usual incomparability assumptions in the absence of nontrivial zero- or one-divisors. On bounded lattices, the closure and interior conditions simplify to explicit identities or image restrictions. Finite proper-trellis examples clarify the role and limitations of the ambient transitivity assumptions.

column6: Invariance and Expressiveness: Modal Variations
column7: This contribution focuses on bisimulation invariance as the hallmark of modal model theory and of modal modelling. It exemplifies traditional as well as more recent ramifications \&\ extensions of classical results -- involving variant modes of bisimulation equivalence and matching modalities also beyond plain Kripke structures, and emphasising especially the technical challenges in finite model theory and other non-elementary settings. Main results to be discussed revolve about the theme of expressive completeness phenomena: beside expressive completeness under bisimulation invariance in relation to first-order background logics, in the style of van Benthem--Rosen characterisations, this also concerns maximality results under criteria form abstract model theory, in the style of Lindstroem theorems.

column6: Multiplicative Sidon basis
column7: For a $h \ge 2$ integer a sequence of positive integers $A$ is called asymptotic basis of order $h$ if every sufficiently large positive integer $n$ can be written as a sum of $h$ elements of $A$. We say a sequence of positive integers $A$ is a multiplicative Sidon sequence if all the products of two elements of the sequence $A$ are distinct. In this paper we prove the existence of a multiplicative Sidon set which is an asymptotic basis of order 2 by using the probabilistic method.

column5: Emiel Claasen; Mehregan Doroudiani; Claude Duhr; Axel Kleinschmidt; Franca Lippert; Oliver Schlotterer; Yoann Sohnle
column6: Equivariant iterated Eisenstein integrals for congruence subgroups of level 2
column7: The modular properties of holomorphic Eisenstein series for $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ and its congruence subgroups do not carry over to their primitives. Instead, the transformation of iterated Eisenstein integrals under congruence subgroups of level $N$ introduces inhomogeneous terms comprising (among others) cyclotomic multiple zeta values of level $N$. We combine iterated Eisenstein integrals for the congruence subgroups of level $N=2$ of arbitrary iteration depth with their complex conjugates and (single-valued) level-2 cyclotomic multiple zeta values such that they define non-holomorphic modular forms. Our construction of these so-called equivariant iterated Eisenstein integrals for $Γ(2)$ and $Γ_0(2)$ proceeds at the level of generating series that take values in an infinite-dimensional (pro-unipotent) Lie group and closely follow Brown's analogous construction in the $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ case. The required insertions of cyclotomic multiple zeta values are controlled by zeta generators for level 2 that normalise the corresponding (pro-nilpotent) Lie algebra of the generating series and whose Lie-bracket relations we determine systematically. Upon restriction to Eisenstein series of modular weight~2, we recover single-valued multiple polylogarithms on the genus 0 modular curve $Γ(2)\backslash \mathbb{H}$.

column6: Quasipolynomial pyjamas
column7: The ``pyjama stripe" $E(\varepsilon)$ is the set of all complex numbers whose real part lies within $\varepsilon$ of the nearest integer. The Pyjama Problem asks whether, for each $\varepsilon > 0$, there exists some union of finitely many rotations of $E(\varepsilon)$ about the origin that covers the plane. This was answered in the affirmative by Manners. Kravitz and Leng subsequently showed that $\exp(\exp(\exp(\varepsilon^{-O(1)})))$ rotations suffice. In this paper, we prove an upper bound of \[\exp((\log \varepsilon^{-1})^{50000})\] rotations. We also show that at least $(π/2 + 0.003 + o(1))\varepsilon^{-1}$ rotations are necessary, improving upon the natural lower bound of $(π/2 + o(1))\varepsilon^{-1}$.
